ܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܘܰܦܪ̈ܝܺܩܺܝܢ ܒܕܰܡ ܝܰܩܺܝܪ ܢܶܙܕܰܗܪܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܢܘܽܪܳܐ ܘܚܶܫܘܽܟܳܝܐ ܒܰܪܳܝܳܝܐ. ܘܰܠܒ̈ܝܺܫܰܝ ܒ݁ܶܪܡܳܢܳܐ ܢܶܬܚܰܠܨܘܽܢ ܚܠܺܝܨܳܐܝܺܬ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܓܘܽܚܟܳܐ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܚܰܒܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ. ܘܕ݂ܰܡܣܰܟ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܩܥܳܬܳܐ ܢܛܰܝܒܘܽܢ ܦܪܳܓܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܣܰܟ݁ܺܝ̈ܢܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܒܬܘܽܠܳܬܳܐ ܣܰܟ݁̈ܠܳܬܳܐ. ܘܰܕܒ݂ܳܢܶܝܢ ܡܰܓ݁ܕ݁ܠܳܐ ܢܶܚܫܒܘܽܢ ܢܶܦ݁ܺܩܳܬܶܗ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܓܘܽܚܟܳܐ ܠܥܳܒܪ̈ܰܝ ܐܘܽܪ̈ܚܳܝܐ. ܘܪܳܥܰܝܘܳܬܳܐ ܢܰܣܺܝ̈ܢ ܢܶܝܣܥܪܘܽܢ ܓܙܳܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܕܰܢܩܰܒܠܘܽܢ ܦܘܽܪܥܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܪܰܒ ܪܳܥܰܘܳܬܳܐ. ܘܰܡܩܰܒܺܠܰܝ ܟܶܣܦܳܝܐ ܢܚܰܘܘܽܢ ܚܘܺܐܪܳܢܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܥܰܒ݁ܺܝܕ݂ܶܐ ܒܝܳܫ̈ܶܐ ܢܶܦܩܘܽܢ ܠܒܰܪܳܝܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܕ݂ܚܠܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܙܰܘ̈ܥܶܐ ܘܓܰܠ̈ܠܶܐ ܕܰܩܝ̈ܡܳܢ. ܘܰܣܘ̈ܒܝ̈ܟܰܝ ܡܶܫܬܘܳܬܳܐ ܢܥܰܬܕܘܽܢ ܪ̈ܘܰܡܚܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܠܒܫܘܽܢ ܢܰܚ̈ܬܳܐ: ܕܢܶܫܘܘܽܢ
Let those who are reborn from the waters and redeemed by the precious blood, beware of the fire and the outer darkness. Let those who have put on the breastplate, gird themselves strenuously, lest they become a mockery to all their companions. Let those who await the cry, adorn their lamps, lest they suffer penury like the foolish virgins. Let those who build a tower, calculate its expenses, lest they be turned into an illusion for those passing by. Let strenuous pastors pay care to their flocks, so that they may obtain a reward from the Prince of pastors. Let those who have received money bring forth profit, lest they be cast into darkness with the wicked servants. Let those who have a sound mind, strip themselves of disease, and not fear the storms or the rising waves. Let those who recline at the banquet, prepare gifts and be adorned with garments, so that they may be held worthy of the bridal chamber. Let those who suffer the yoke, endure reproach. Let the prudent virgins prepare their lamps.
ܠܶܗ ܠܰܓܢܘܳܢܳܐ. ܘܰܟܩ̈ܰܒܳܠܰܝ ܢܝܳܪܳܐ ܢܣܰܝܒܪܘܽܢ ܚܣܕܳܐ. ܘܰܒܬܘ̈ܽܠܳܬܳܐ ܚܰܟܺܝ̈ܡܳܬܳܐ ܢܛܰܝܒ̈ܳܢ ܫܪܳܓܰܝܗܶܝܢ܀ ܢܰܕ݂ܪܶܟ݂ ܢܰܦܫܰܢ ܚܰܒܺܝ̈ܒܰܝܢ ܒܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܘܰܒܠܶܐܘܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܫܰܗܪܳܐ ܘܰܒܒܳܥܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܨܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܒܰܨܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܬܰܟ݂ܫܶܦܬ݁ܳܐ ܚܢܺܝܚܬܳܐ: ܕ݁ܰܠܡܳܐ ܒܰܥܓܰܠ ܢܶܬܕܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܘܢܶܬܚܰܝܰܒ ܒܕ݂ܝܳܢܶܗ ܟܺܐܢܳܝܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܢܶܒܣܶܐ ܒܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܩܰܕ݁ܺܝܫܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܢܰܢ ܢܶܣܬܠܶܐ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܰܡܺܝܪ
17. Let us humble ourselves, most beloved, with labor, fatigue, vigils, supplication, fasting, prayer, and entreaty with groans, lest, being suddenly taken from this world, we be condemned by the just judgment of God. For we ought not to spurn the ministry of the Holy One, lest we also be rejected by Him, just as He said through the prophet: 'Because you have rejected the law of God,'
ܒܰܫܒܺܝܠܳܐ: ܕܥܰܠ ܕܐܰܣܠܺܝܬ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܶܗ ܕ݁ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܰܣܠܺܝܟ ܡܶܢ ܟܳܗܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܬܘܽܒ
I will cast you out from the priesthood. It is written again: Those who glorify me, I will glorify; but those who despise me shall be held in contempt.


[p. 614] {#po.0.p614}
ܢܶܨܛܰܥܪܘܽܢ܀ ܚܙܰܘ ܕܝܢ ܡܺܝܢܳܐ ܦܘܽܪܥܳܢܳܐ ܩܰܒ݁ܶܠܘ ܟ݁ܳܗܢܶܐ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܒ݂ܣܰܝܘ ܒܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܶܗ:
18. Consider, moreover, what retribution the priests received who despised His ministry. Nadab and Abihu, holy priests, clothed in the ephod, covered with the breastplate, girded with fine linen, adorned with purple,
ܢܳܕܳܒ ܘܰܐܒܺܝܗܘܽܕ݂ ܟܳܗܢܶܐ ܩܰܕܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܘܰܠܒܺܝ̈ܫܰܝ ܐܺܝܦܘܽܕ݂ ܘܰܡܚܰܦܰܝ̈ ܒܘܽܨܳܐ ܘܰܡܨܰܒܬܰܝ̈ ܒܐܰܪ̈ܓܘܳܢܶܐ ܘܣܳܝܡܰܝ̈ ܟܠܺܝܠܶܐ ܘܟ݁ܰܠܰܘ̈ܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܨܢܰܦܬܳܐ: ܡܩܰܕ݁ܒ݁ܰܚ ܩܘܽܪ̈ܒܳܢܶܐ ܘܰܡܚܰܣܺܝܰܝ ܐ݈ܝܺܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܘܡܰܠܶܦܰܝ ܥܰܡܳܐ ܘܡܩܰܕ݁̈ܫ̈ܰܝ ܟܢܘܽܫܬܳܐ: ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܩܰܠܝܶܠ ܥܘܢܺܝܕܘܳܬܳܐ ܥܶܠܰܬ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܒܣܰܝܘ ܒܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܩܰܕ݁ܺܝܫܳܝܐ ܘܐܰܥܶܠܘ ܢܘܽܪܳܐ ܢܘܽܟܪܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܒܙܰܒܢܳܗ: ܩܶܝܕ݂ܰܬ ܢܘܽܪܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܦܝܳܪ̈ܡܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܐܰܘܩܕ݂ܰܬ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܘܐܰܦ݁ܰܩܘ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܫܪܝܺܬܳܐ. ܘܠܳܐ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܢܳܕܳܒ ܘܐܰܒܺܝܗܘܽܕ݂: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܚܳܦܢܺܝ ܘܦܺܝܢܚܳܣ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܥܺܠܝܽ ܟܳܗܢܳܐ: ܥܰܠ ܕܝܰܩܰܪܘ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܦܩܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܟܩܰܠܘ ܙܶܕ݂ܩܳܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܡܳܝܐ ܝܰܥܢܳܝܳܐܝܺܬ: ܘܨܰܥܰܪܘ ܢܶܫ̈ܶܐ ܕܰܡܨܰܠܝܳܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܝ̈ ܒܡܰܫܟܰܢܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ: ܘܥܺܠܝܰ ܐܵܒܘܽܗܘܽܢ ܠܳܐ ܟܐܳܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܙܥܝ̈ܦܳܐܝܺܬ ܘܰܚܠܺܝܨܳܐܝܺܬ: ܐܶܠܶܐ ܪܰܦܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܘܰܢܫܺܝܫܳܐܝܺܬ ܟܐܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܫܡܰܥ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܶܗ ܥܰܡܐ ܕ݂ܪܳܝܒܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕܒܺܝܫܳܐܝܺܬ ܟܳܗܢܶܐ ܡܰܠ̈ܦܳܢܶܐ ܡܶܬܕܰܒܪܝܺܢ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܩܪܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ
wearing crowns, miters, and tiaras, offering sacrifices, expiating Israel, teaching the people, and sanctifying the assembly, were seized by a sudden blindness, despised the ministry of the Holy One, and brought strange fire at an unseasonable time; therefore, fire bursting forth from their censers devoured them; and they took them up and cast them outside the camp. And not only Nadab and Abihu, but also Hophni and Phinehas, the sons of Eli the priest, when they honored themselves more than the ministry committed to them, and greedily stole offerings from the people, and brought disgrace upon the women who were praying in the tabernacle—yet Eli, their father, did not rebuke them sharply and vehemently, but scolded them lazily and sluggishly, hearing the whole people complaining that the priest-teachers were behaving very badly; and having called them, he said: 'My sons, what is this rumor that I'


[p. 615] {#po.0.p615}


[p. 616] {#po.0.p616}


[p. 617] {#po.0.p617}
ܫܶܡܥܳܝܐ ܗܳܢܐ ܕܫܳܡܰܥ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܥܠܰܝܟܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܶܗ ܥܰܡܳܐ ܕܰܡܕ݂ܰܥܪܝܺܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܠܥܰܡܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ܆ ܐܳܐ ܒܢܰܝ̈: ܠܳܐ ܫܰܦܝܰܪ ܫܶܡܥܳܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܕܫܳܡܰܥ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܥܠܰܝܟܘܽܢ. ܐܶܢ ܠܰܡ ܓ݁ܰܒܪܳܐ ܒܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܢܶܚܛܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܒܳܥܶܐ. ܐܶܢ ܒܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܢܶܚܛܶܐ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܢ ܢܶܒܥܶܐ܆ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܟܐܳܬܳܐ ܣܰܓܺܝܐܬܳܐ ܕܥܶܠܝ ܥܰܠ ܒܢܰܘ̈ܗܝ ܥܒ݂ܰܕ ܘܫܰܬܶܩ.
hear about you from all the people, that you are harassing the people of God with insults? By no means, my sons; this rumor that I hear about you is not at all becoming. If a man sins against a man, he shall pray to the Lord; but if a man sins against the Lord, who shall pray for him?' This was the sluggish correction that Eli used with his sons, and afterwards he was silent; they, however, did not receive amendment from his rebuke. O Eli, high priest of the people! When your sons, wicked men, did not obey you, it was utterly unbecoming for you to be a participant in the crimes
ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܶܝܢ ܒܟܐܳܬܶܗ ܡܰܪܕܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܩܰܒܶܠܘ. ܐܘܽܝ ܥܶܠܝ ܟܳܗܢܳܝܐ ܪܺܫܳܝܐ ܕܥܰܡܳܐ܆ ܟܰܕ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܡܥܝܺܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܟ ܓܰܒܪ̈ܶܐ ܪ̈ܰܫܝ̈ܥܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܘܳܠܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܟܳܗܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܡܕܰܒ݁ܰܪܬ ܘܰܠܘܳܬ ܕܐܶܫܬܰܘܬܰܦ݂
that your sons were committing! It is clear, indeed, that he rebuked them out of respect for the people, but not from his heart.
ܠܰܚܛܳܗܰܝܗܶܝܢ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܟ ܣܳܥܪܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܰܕ݂ܝܳܐ ܗܳܝ ܕܰܠܥܰܝܢܰܝ̈ ܥܰܡܳܐ ܟܐܳܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܠܶܒܶܗ܀ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܙܰܗܪܰܢ ܦܳܪܘܽܩܰܢ: ܕܐܶܢ ܥܰܝܢܳܟ݂ ܡܰܟܫܠܳܐ ܠܳܟ݂ ܚܕܳܝܳܐ ܫܕ݂ܺܝܗ ܡܶܢܳܟ: ܐܰܘ ܐܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܪܶܓܠܳܐ: ܕܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܲܢܘܽܢ ܗܰܕܳܡܶܐ ܕ݁ܢܰܩܫܺܝܪܝܺܢ ܒ݁ܦ݁ܰܓ݂ܪܳܐ ܥܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܚܳܙܝܳܐ ܘܐܝܺܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܥܳܡܠܳܐ ܘܪܶܓܠܳܐ ܕܰܡܗܰܠܟܳܐ: ܘܐܳܦܶܢ ܠܰܡ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܗܰܕ݁ܳܡ̈ܶܐ ܡܰܟܫܠܺܝܢ ܠܳܟ݂ ܦܣܘܽܩ ܫܕܺܝ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢܳܟ: ܘܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܶܢ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܗܘܶܐ. ܐܳܦ ܡܘܽܫܶܝܐ ܙܰܗܰܪ ܐܰܝܟ ܦܳܪܘܽܩܰܢ: ܕܐܶܢ ܒܪܳܟ݂ ܐܰܘ ܒܰܪܬ݁ܳܟ݂ ܐܰܘ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܬ݂ ܩܝܳܡܳܟ݂ ܐܰܘ ܪܰܚܡܳܟ ܕܐܰܝܟ݂ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ:
19. Therefore our Savior warned us: 'If your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it from you'; and likewise your hand or your foot, which are the most excellent members in the body—namely, the eye that sees, the hand that labors, and the foot that walks; if these very members cause you to stumble, cut them off and cast them from you, so that you may not be barred from life alone. Moses also gave the same commandment as the Savior: 'If your son or your daughter, or the wife of your covenant, or your friend who is to you as your own soul, if, I say, one of these invites you'
ܐܶܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܢܓ݂ܰܪܓܳܟ ܘܢܺܐܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ: ܕܰܫܒܘܽܩ ܠܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܘܬܳܐ ܢܺܐܙܰܠ ܢܶܦܠܘܽܚ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܶܐ ܐ̱ܚܪ̈ܳܢܶܐ: ܠܳܐ ܬܶܫܡܰܥ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܶܬܛܦܝ݁ܣ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܚܘܽܣ ܘܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܟܰܣܶܐ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒܟܺܐܦ݁ܶܐ ܢܶܬܪܰܓܡܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܘܒܕܽܘܢ. ܕܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܒܪܳܐ ܘܒܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܐܰܢ̱ܬܬ݂ ܛܰܠܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܗܰܕܳܡ̈ܶܐ ܚܰܒܺܝ̈ܒܶܐ ܥܰܝܢܳܐ ܘܐܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܘܪܶܓܠܳܐ ܕ݁ܚܰܝܳܝܺܝܢ ܘܚܰܒܺܝܒܺܝܢ ܒ݁ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܦܰܓܪܳܐ. ܘܦܳܪܘܽܩܰܢ ܬܘܽܒ ܐܰܠܶܦ: ܕܡܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܳܚܺܡ ܠܺܝ ܝܰܬܺܝܪ ܡܶܢ ܕܠܰܐܒܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܘܠܶܐܡܶܗ ܘܝܰܬܺܝܪ ܡܶܢ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ: ܬܰܠܡܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܠܡܶܗܘܳܐ ܠܺܝ. ܘܡܘܽܫܶܝܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܰܪܚܰܡ ܠܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܟ݂ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ ܘܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܚܰܝܠܳܟ݂ ܘܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܶܗ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܳܟ݂. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܰܠܶܦܘܽܢ ܟܬܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܩܰܕܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ: ܕܢܶܬܚܰܦܰܛ ܒܝܗܶܝܢ ܕܢܶܬܪܰܚܡܰܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܢܰܥܠܰܢ ܠܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܶܗ ܡܚܰܩܰܪܬܳܐ܀
saying to you: 'Let us forsake the Lord; come, let us go and serve strange gods'; do not listen to them, nor acquiesce, nor spare them, nor hide them; but let them be overwhelmed with stones, and let them perish. Furthermore, a son and a daughter and the wife of one's youth are precious members, namely, the eye, the hand, or the foot, the most excellent and dearest in the whole body. Again our Savior taught us: 'He who does not love me more than his father or his mother, or more than his own soul, cannot be my disciple.' Again Moses says: 'Love the Lord your God with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your faculty.' These things the Holy Scriptures teach us, so that we may strive, with their help, to be loved by God and introduced into His most excellent kingdom.


[p. 618] {#po.0.p618}
ܡܶܛܽܠ ܥܰܘܠܗܘܽܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܰܗܪܘܽܢ ܠܒ̈ܘܫܰܝ ܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܳܐ ܐܶܬܦ݁ܪܶܫܘܽ ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܫܪܝܺܬܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܰܝܘܣܳܢ ܒ݁ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܛܰܡܳܐܐ: ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܥܰܘܠܳܐ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܥܺܰܠܝܽ ܢܦܰܠ ܥܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܺܝܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܒ݁ܚܰܪܒ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܦܠܶܫ̈ܬܳܝܶܐ: ܘܐܶܬܕܰܒܪܰܬ ܩܺܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܕܺܝܰܬܺܩܺܐ: ܘܐܰܥܠܘܽܗ ܠܶܐܫܕ݁ܘܰܕ݂ ܠܒܶܝܬ ܕ݁ܰܓ݂ܽܘܢ ܒܰܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܛܰܡܳܐܐ. ܘܐܘܽܒ ܐܳܦ ܥܺܘܙܳܐ ܟ݁ܳܗܢܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܕܰܒܣܳܐ ܒܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܩܺܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܕ݁ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܢܰܩܶܦ ܒܶܗ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܬܘܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܡܺܝܬ.
20. For, because of their sins, the sons of Aaron, clothed in sacred [vestments], were mercilessly cast outside the camp into a polluted place. Because of the sins of the sons of Eli, the people of Israel fell by the sword of the Philistines, the ark of the covenant was carried away, and it was brought into Ashdod, into the temple of Dagon, an unclean seat. Again, the Lord struck Oza the priest with a plague when he despised the ministry of the ark of the Lord, and he died. But what, beloved, was this contempt of Oza? It was that he brought the ark on a cart, transgressing the law,
ܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܚܰܒܺܝܒܰܝ̈ ܒܶܣܚܳܢܶܗ ܕܥܺܘܙܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܕܰܫܩܰܠ ܩܺܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܒܥܳܓܰܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܥܒܰܪ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܘܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܦ݂ܩܶܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܡܘܽܫܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܟܰܕ݂ ܩܰܪܶܒܘ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܕܐܺܝܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܩܘܽܪ̈ܒ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܕܚܘܰܕ݁ܳܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܫܟܰܢ ܙܰܒܢܳܝܐ ܬܰܘܪܶܐ ܘܥܰܓ݂̈ܠܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܩܰܕ݁ܺܝܫܳܐ ܠܡܘܽܫܶܐ ܥܰܒܕܶܗ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܕܣܰܒ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܗܰܒ ܠܠܶܘ̈ܳܝ̈ܐ ܕܢܶܦܠܚܘܽܢ ܒܗܶܝܢ ܒܥܰܓ݂ܠܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܦܘܽܠܚܳܢܳܐ ܒܡܰܫܟ݁ܰܢ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܝܐ ܘܢܶܫܩܠܘ̇ܢ ܒܡܳܓ݂ܠܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܟ݀ܽܠܳܗ ܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܡܰܫܟܰܢ ܙܰܒܢ̈ܳܝܐ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ: ܕܗܰܒ ܠܰܒ̈ܢܰܝ ܓܶܪܫܘܽܢ ܡܶܢܬܶܬ ܦܘܽܠܚܳܢܗܘܽܢ: ܘܠܰܒ̈ܢܰܝ ܩܳܗܳܬ ܠܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܬܶܠ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܦܘܽܠܚܳܢܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܳܐ ܡܰܫܠܰܡ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܥܰܠ ܟܰܬܦܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܢܶܫܩܠܘܽܢ ܒܐܝܺܩܳܪܳܐ ܘܰܒܙܰܗܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ. ܝܳܕ݂ܥܺܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܢ ܕܩܺܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܕܺܝܰܬܺܩܺܝܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܡܬܘܽܡ ܐܶܫܬܰܩܠܰܬ ܥܰܠ ܥܳܓܰܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܗܘܽ ܙܰܒܢܳܐ ܟܰܕ݂ ܫܰܕ݂ܪܘܽܗ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܕܰܦܠܶܫ̈ܬ݁ܳܝܶܐ ܘܣܳܡܘܽܗ ܥܰܠ ܥܳܓܰܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܟܰܕ݂ ܢܰܓ݁ܰܪܘ ܠܳܗ ܬ݁ܰܘܪ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܬܰܪ̈ܬܶܝܢ ܕܰܚܠܺܝܒܳܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܗܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪܗܶܝܢ. ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܩܰܒ݁ܶܠܘ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܝܺܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܠܩܺܒܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܰܚܬܘܽܗ ܠܶܘܳܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܓܰܠܬ݁ܳܐ: ܟܰܕ݂ ܫܰܕ݂ܪܘܽܗ
and acting against the precept of Moses. For when the princes of Israel had offered gifts at the dedication of the tabernacle, namely, oxen and carts, the Lord commanded Moses His servant, saying: 'Take them from them, and give them to the Levites, so that they may use the carts for the service of the tabernacle, so that they may transport all the ministry of the tabernacle in them.' But He said to him: 'Give them to the sons of Gershon according to the necessity of their ministry; but you shall not give them to the sons of Kohath, who will carry the ministry of the sanctuary, enjoined upon them, on their own shoulders for the sake of honor, dignity, and glory.' You know, brothers, that the ark of the covenant had not yet been carried on a cart when the satraps of the Philistines, returning it, placed it on a cart to which they yoked two cows, which were followed by weaned calves. And when the sons of Israel received the ark, the Levites took it down from the cart on which the Philistines had returned it, and placed it in the house of Abinadab in Gibeah. But in the same way, they also wanted to carry it, and not on their own shoulders, as the Most Holy had commanded Moses, and Moses had handed down to the priests. Oza also did not notice that when Joshua the son of Nun crossed the Jordan, God


[p. 619] {#po.0.p619}


[p. 620] {#po.0.p620}
ܕܰܒܓܶܒܥܬܳܐ. ܒܗ ܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܙܳܐ ܨܳܒ݂ܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕ݁ܰܗܘܰܘ ܫܳܩܠܺܝܢ ܠܳܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܟܰܬܦܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܩܰܕܺܝܫܳܐ ܠܡܘܽܫܶܐ ܘܡܘܽܫܶܐ ܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܠܟܳܗܢ̈ܶܝܐ. ܘܥܳܙܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܟ݁ܰܠ ܕܐܳܦ݂ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܒܰܪܢܘܽܢ ܟܰܕ݂ ܥܒܰܪ ܝܘܽܪܕ݂ܢܳܢ ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܦܰܩܕ݁ܶܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܕܢܶܫܩܠܘܽܢ ܟܳܗܢܶܐ ܠܩܺܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܢܺܐܙܠ̱ܘܽܢ ܩܕܳܡ ܥܰܡܳܐ ܘܢܶܬܦܠܶܓ ܝܘܽܪܕ݂ܢܳܢ: ܘܰܫܩܰܠܘ ܟܽܠܶܗ ܥܰܡܳܐ. ܡܶܢ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܐܶܣܬܰܟ݂ܰܠ ܥܳܙܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܟܺܐܢܳܐܝܺܬ ܕܝܺܢܳܐ ܒܪܘܺܓ݁ܙܳܐ ܩܰܒܶܠ. ܘܕ݂ܰܘܺܝܕ݂ ܟܰܕ݂ ܚܙܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܡܚܳܐ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܬܘܰܪܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܥܳܙܳܐ ܕܚܶܠ ܠܡܰܥܳܠܘܽ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܠܩܺܝܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܰܥܠܘܽܗ ܠܒܶܝܬ ܥܘܽܒܶܕ݂ ܐܵܕܘܽܡ ܓܳܬܳܝܳܝܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܥܘܽܒܶܕ݂ ܐܵܕܘܽܡ ܡܶܢ ܓ݁ܳܬ ܘܗܳܐ ܕܰܦܠܳܫ̈ܬܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܡܳܐ ܛܰܡܳܐܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܐܝܺܣܪܳܝܝܶܠ. ܘܺܝܕ݂ܰܥ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕܡܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܝܰܩܰܪ ܠܩܺܝܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܳܠܰܥ ܒܟܰܐܦ̈ܶܐ ܡܰܕܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܒܡܰܚܺܘܳܬܳܐ ܒܺܝܫ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܒܠܰܒܘ ܦܠܶܫ̈ܬ݁ܳܝܶܐ ܒܰܛܚܘܽܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܐܰܝܠܶܠܘ ܥܰܩܪܽܘܢܳܝܶܐ ܘܐܶܩܰܡܪܘ: ܕܰܠܓ݁ܳܬ ܬ݁ܺܐܙܰܠ ܩܺܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ. ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܥܘܽܒܶܕ݂ ܐܵܕܘܽܡ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܕܒܰܪܘ ܦܠܳܫ̈ܬܳܝܶܐ ܒܗܰܘ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ ܕܰܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܩܘܽܪܒܳܢܳܐ ܠܩܺܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܐܶܬ݂ܩܛܶܠܘ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܥܺܠܝܽ ܚܳܦܢܝܺ ܘܦܺܝܢܚܳܣ ܟܳܗܢܶܐ ܡܨܰܥܪ̈ܰܝ ܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܰܕ݂ܚܶܠܘ ܦܠܶܫ̈ܬܳܝܶܐ ܘܢܰܝܩܰܪܘ ܠܩܺܝܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܐܳܦ ܟܰܕ݂ ܫܰܕܪܘܽܗ ܒܩܘܽܙ̈ܒܳܢܶܐ ܫܰܕܪܘܽܗ: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܪܰܒ݁ܳܐ ܚܫܝܺܒܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ ܒܥܰܝܢܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܺܝܡ ܟܰܕ݂ ܚܙܰܐܘܽܗ ܕܐܶܬܳܬ ܠܡܰܫܪܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ: ܘܺܝ ܠܰܢ܆ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܗܳܐ ܐܶܬܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܡܰܫܪܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܥܶܒܪ̈ܳܢܶܝܐ. ܐܶܬܚܰܝܰܠܘ ܦܠܶܫ̈ܬܳܝܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܗܳܢܰܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܐܰܘܒܶܕ݂ ܠܡܶܨܪܶܝܢ ܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܡܰܚܺܘܳܢ܂
had commanded: 'The priests shall carry the ark, and they shall go before the people, and the Jordan shall be divided'; and all the people crossed. From this at least Oza was instructed, and therefore he justly and deservedly bore the judgment of wrath. But David, seeing that the Lord had struck Oza with that blow, feared to bring the ark of God to himself; therefore they brought it into the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite, because Obed-Edom was from Gath of the Philistines, from a polluted people, and not from Israel; and consequently he knew that a man who did not honor the ark of God would be punished with most grievous pains and worst plagues, just as the Philistines were struck with hemorrhoids, and the Ekronites wailed, saying: 'Let the ark return to Gath.' From then on, Obed-Edom knew that the Philistines had given a gift when they sent out the ark. The sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas the priests, despisers of the ministry, were killed; but the Philistines feared, and honored the ark of God; and even when they sent it back, they followed it with gifts; and it was regarded in their eyes as a kind of great divinity. For previously, seeing it arrive in the camp, they said: 'Woe to us, for behold, God has come into the camp of the Hebrews. Be strong, Philistines, for this is the God who destroyed Egypt with all the plagues.'


[p. 621] {#po.0.p621}


[p. 622] {#po.0.p622}


[p. 623] {#po.0.p623}


[p. 624] {#po.0.p624}
ܘܰܚܙܰܘ ܚܰܒ̈ܝܒܰܝܢ ܕܥܘܰܒܶܕ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܓܳܬܳܝܳܐ ܡܛܠ ܕܥܶܠܰܬ ܠܒܰܝܬܶܗ ܩܺܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܶܬ݁ܰܪܰܟ. ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܐܰܣܩܳܝܗ ܕܰܘܺܝܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܒܶܝܬ ܥܘܰܒܶܕ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܠܰܩܪܝܺܬܳܐ ܕܨܲܗܝܘܽܢ ܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܠܟܳܗܢܶܐ ܘܫܰܩܠܘܽܗ ܥܰܠ ܟܰܬܦܳܬܗܘܽܢ. ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܕܰܘܺܝܕ݂ ܡܗܰܠܶܟ݂ ܒܪܶܓ݁ܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܚܳܝܕ݁ܶܐ ܙܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܘܡܶܫܬܥܳܐ ܩܕܳܡ ܩܺܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܰܥܝܩܰܬ
See also, most beloved, that Obed-Edom the Gittite, because the ark of God entered his house, obtained a blessing. And when David brought it from the house of Obed-Edom into the city of Zion, he prescribed for the priests that they should carry it on their shoulders. And while he himself was walking on foot and rejoicing and dancing before the ark, Michal the daughter of Saul despised him.
ܒܗ ܡܰܠܟ݁ܰܠ ܒܰܪܰܬ ܫܳܐܘܽܠ܀ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܚܰܒ̈ܝܒܰܝܢ ܕܐܶܠܨܰܬ ܠܰܢ ܠܡܶܟܬܰܒ݂: ܕܢܰܚܥܺܝܕ݂ ܢܰܦܫܰܝܢ ܐܳܦ ܠܟܘܢ ܕܥܰܠ ܕܰܒܣܰܝܢ ܒܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܶܗ ܩܰܕ݁ܝܺܫܳܐ ܓܕܰܫ ܠܰܢ ܗܳܠܺܝܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܒܗܳܢܳܐ ܙܰܒܢܳܐ. ܥܰܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܰܩܰܪܢܳܝ ܗ̱ܝ ܝܰܗܒ݁ܰܢ ܠܡܘܽܝܳܩܳܐ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܒܥܶܠܕ݁݁ܒܳܒܰܝܢ ܘܐܰܫܚܺܝܛܰܝܢ ܐܰܟ ܕܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܳܫܺܝܘܽܛܳܝ ܢܶܨܛܰܥܪܘܽܢ܀
21. It was necessary for us, most beloved, to write these things down, so that we might recall to our memory and yours that all those things happened to us at this time because we despised the ministry of the Holy One. Because we did not honor Him, He handed us over to the derision of our enemies, and brought us into contempt, just as He said: 'Those who despise me shall become ignoble.'
ܚܫܶܟܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܘܰܒܕܰܚܝܢ ܒܝܰܪܡܝܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܰܙܦܿܳܬ݂ܰܢ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܛܰܡܝܡܰܬ ܡܰܟܘܽܥܰܫ ܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ: ܘܥܶܪ̈ܫ݁ܰܝ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܬܚܥܶܟܘ ܒܚܰܕ݂ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܪܶܡܘܽܬܳܐ: ܥܶܠܰܬ݂ ܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܒܥܰܕ݁ܳܠܳܐ ܕܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܒܶܐܟܘܽܠܬܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܚܛܳܐ ܐܳܕ݁ܶܡ ܘܰܢܦ݁ܰܩ ܡܶܢ ܟܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ. ܫܒܰܩ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܩܰܕ݁ܺܝܫܳܐ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܰܝ̈ ܦ݁ܰܪܕܺܝܣܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܢܳܛܥܺܝܢ ܐܶܒܳܚܐ ܒܪܝܺܟܿܳܐ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܕܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܬܶܐܟܘܽܠ:
22. For pride darkened our minds, greed destroyed us, and contaminated the fountains of wisdom. The roots of doctrine were extinguished by avarice and elation. Sin entered the world through the enticement of greed, when, namely, by eating from the tree, Adam sinned and went out of paradise. The Most Holy had indeed left all the trees of paradise before Adam, bringing forth blessed fruits, and had said to him: 'Of all you shall eat; but of the tree of the knowledge of good and
ܒܪܰܡ ܕܺܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܐܝܺܠܳܢ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܛܳܒܬܳܐ ܘܰܕܒܺܝܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܐܟ݂ܘܽܠ ܡܶܢܶܝܗ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܡܘܽܬ. ܘܠܳܐ ܣܦܰܩ ܠܚܰܥܢܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܰܠܶܗ ܦܰܪܕܺܝܣܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܪܘܝܺܚ ܘܰܡܚܰܬܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕ݂ܗܳܫܳܐ ܙܪܝܺܥܝܺܢ ܒܳܗ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܘܰܠܚܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܥܬܝܺܕܝܺܢ ܟܽܠ ܙܰܕ݁ܺܝܩܶܐ ܕܒܿܳܗ ܢܶܬܬܢܺܝܚܘܽܢ ܒܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ ܕܡܶܫܬܩܶܠ ܟܘܽܠܛܳܢܳܐ ܕܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܰܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܦܳܪܘܺܩܰܢ ܠܰܕ݂ܡܶܢ ܝܰܡܺܝܢܶܗ: ܕܐܰܡܺܝܢ ܐܶܡܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܳܟ݂: ܕܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܫܰܡܝܚ ܬܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܓ݂ܰܢܰܬ ܥܕܶܢ. ܘܐܘܽܦ ܟܬܝܒ ܒܰܢܒܺܝܳܐ: ܕܙܰܕ̈ܝܺܩܶܐ ܝܺܪܬܺܝܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܢܳܙܶܝܢ ܥ݁ܠܺܝܗ ܠܥܳܠܰܡ. ܘܠܳܐ ܝܳܪܬܺܝܢ ܠܳܗ ܠܕܳܪܕܳܪܺܝܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܡܶܥܒܰܪ ܥܳܒܪܳܐ ܐܰܟ ܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ: ܕܰܫܡܰܝܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܬ݁ܶܢܳܢܳܐ ܢܶܥܒܪܘܽܢ: ܘܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܟ ܠܒܘܽܫܶܐ ܬܶܒܠܶܐ. ܘܐܳܦ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܰܫܡܰܝܐ ܘܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܢܶܥܒܪܘܽܢ: ܘܡܶܠܰܝ ܠܳܐ ܢܶܥܒܕܳܢ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܫܡܰܝܐ ܕܰܠܥُܠ ܡܶܢܰܢ ܡܶܬܩܪܺܝܢ ܪܩܺܝܥܳܐ ܥܒܪܝܺܢ: ܘܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܗܝܺ ܝܰܒܺܝܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܳܠܝܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܰܚܝܶܐ ܘܰܫܡܰܝܐ ܕܰܠܥُܠ ܡܶܢ ܪܩܺܝܥܳܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܒܳܠܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܪܝܺܢ܀
evil you shall not eat, lest you die.' Nor was the whole of paradise sufficient for his greed, the whole earth more spacious and excellent, in which today the sons of Adam are dispersed; but in the end, when the empire of greed has been taken away, the just who are in it will obtain rest, just as the Savior said to him who was on the right: 'Amen I say to you: Today you will be with me in paradise.' Again it is written in the prophet: 'The just shall inherit the earth, and shall dwell upon it forever.' But they shall not inherit it for perpetual generations; since it will pass away at some time, as it is written: 'The heavens shall vanish like smoke, and the earth shall wither like a garment.' Again our Lord says: 'Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.' This heaven which is above us, and is called the firmament, shall pass away, and this earth, which is called the dry land, shall pass away; but the earth of life, and the heavens which are above the firmament, shall not wither nor pass away.


[p. 625] {#po.0.p625}


[p. 626] {#po.0.p626}
ܘܗܝܺ ܟܽܠܳܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܗܰܘ ܟܽܠܶܗ ܟܰܪܕܺܝܣܳܐ ܠܶܐ ܣܒܰܩ ܠܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܥܶܠܰܬ݂ ܥܰܠ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܪܰܓܪܰܓ ܕܐܳܦ݂ ܡܶܢ ܕܐܶܬܦܩܶܕ݂ ܢܶܣܰܒ ܘܢܶܐܟܘܽܠ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܥܺܣܘܽ ܙܰܒܶܢ ܒܘܽܟܪܘܽܬܶܗ: ܘܐܶܣܬܠܺܝ ܐܳܦ ܡܶܢ ܒܘܽܪܟܬܳܐ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܶܗ ܕܦܶܪܥܘܽܢ
23. Therefore this whole earth, and all that paradise, did not suffice for the greed that came upon Adam, so much so that against the commandment he coveted to take and eat. Similarly, because of greed, Esau sold his birthright, but he was also rejected from the blessing. Because of


[p. 627] {#po.0.p627}


[p. 628] {#po.0.p628}
ܚܶܪܒܰܬ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܡܶܨܪܶܝܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܣܦ݁ܰܩ ܠܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܶܗ ܟܽܠܶܗ ܥܰܡܳܐ ܕܰܡܕܰܒܰܪ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܘܐܳܦ ܠܐܝܺܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܨܒܳܐ ܠܶܡܟܰܒܰܫ ܒܥܰܒܕ݂ܘܳܬܳܐ. ܘܐܳܦ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܰܗܪܘܽܢ ܕܐܶܬܝܰܥܰܢܘ ܐܶܣܬܠܺܝܘ ܡܶܢ ܟܳܗܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܝܺܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܕܰܪܓ݂ܘ ܡܶܐܟܘܽܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܒܰܙܒܰܢ ܙܒܰܢ ܣܠܶܩ ܒܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܪܘܺܓ݁ܙܳܐ ܡܰܘܬܳܢܳܝܐ ܘܰܚܘܰܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܚܰܘ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܛܽܘܪ̈ܦܳܢܳܝܳܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܓܢܺܝܣ ܓܢܺܝܣ. ܘܐܳܦ ܥܳܟܳܪ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܙܶܕܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܶܬ݁ܪܓܶܡ܂ ܒܟܺܐܦ݁ܶܐ ܘܐܳܒܰܕ ܡܶܢ ܓܰܘ ܥܰܡܶܗ. ܘܟܳܗܢܶܐ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܥܺܠܝܽ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܰܘܒܕ݂ܰܬ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܰܝܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ. ܘܫܳܐܘܳܠ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܓܰܒܝܳܝܐ ܕܥܰܡܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܕܐܶܬܝܰܥܰܢ ܒܚܶܪܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܥܡܳܠܺܝܩ ܢܦܰܠ ܡܶܢ ܪܰܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܐܶܨܛܰܪܝܰܬ ܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܶܗ. ܘܐܳܦ ܐܰܚܳܒ ܒܪܶܗ ܕܥܰܡܪܺܝ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܪܓ݂ܰܬ ܘܰܢܣܰܒ ܟܰܪܡܶܗ ܕܢܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܰܢܦܰܠ ܒܰܩܪܳܒܳܐ ܒܪܳܡܰܬ ܓܶܠܥܳܕ݂. ܘܓܰܚܙܝܺ ܬܘܒ ܬܰܠܡܺܝܕ݁ܶܗ ܕܐܶܠܝܫܰܥ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܶܗ ܓܰܪܒ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܠܒܶܫܬܶܗ. ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܩܶܛܠܰܬ ܣܰܓ݁ܺܝ̈ܐܶܐ ܘܣܰܝܪܩܰܬ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܰܝܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ. ܝܺܗܘܽܕܳܐ ܐܶܣܟܰܪܝܽܘܽܛܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܬ݁ܪܶܥܣܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܣܰܒܥܰܬ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܶܗ ܕܰܓܙܰܒ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܢܶܣܰܒ ܕܡܰܫ ܝܰܩܺܝܪܳܐ: ܘܒܳܗ ܒܫܰܝܕܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܶܬܦܪܶܫ ܡܶܢ ܬܰܠܡܺܝܕܶܐ ܚܰܒܪ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܐܳܦ ܠܚܰܢܰܢܳܐ ܙܟܳܬ݂ܶܗ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܐܶܬܚܰܙܝܰܬ ܒ݁ܶܗ ܬܶܕ݂ܡܘܽܪܬ݁ܳܐ
Pharaoh's greed, the land of Egypt was devastated; for the whole people he ruled did not suffice for his greed, but he also wanted to oppress Israel with servitude. The sons of Aaron also conceived covetousness; but they were rejected from the priesthood. The Israelites, who greedily desired food more frequently, were attacked by deadly wrath, with serpents and other plagues of various kinds. Achan also was overwhelmed with stones because of the lust of avarice, and perished from the midst of his people. And greed deprived the sons of Eli, the impious priests, of life. Saul likewise, chosen king of the people, because he coveted the anathema of the Amalekites, fell from a higher place, and his kingdom was cut off. Likewise Ahab, son of Omri, king of Israel, desired and seized the vineyard of Naboth; but he fell in battle in Ramoth-Gilead. Gehazi, the disciple of Elisha, was also covered with leprosy by his greed. Greed killed many and defrauded them of life. The avidity of Judas Iscariot, [one] of the twelve, was not satisfied by thefts, until he even stole the price of the Most Precious One, and by his greed was removed from the disciples, his companions. Avarice also overcame Ananias, and the prodigy was manifested in him before the feet of the apostles.
ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܪܶܓ݂ܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕܰܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ܀ ܠܳܐ ܣܳܦܶܩ ܠܳܗ ܠܚܰܡܢܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ
24. The whole world does not suffice for avarice.


[p. 629] {#po.0.p629}


[p. 630] {#po.0.p630}
ܐܰܬܪܶܗ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܣܳܦܶܩ ܠܶܗ. ܟܳܢܫܝܺܢ ܚܰܝܳܠܶܐ ܘܥܳܒܕ݁ܝܺܢ ܩܪ̈ܳܒ݁ܶܐ: ܡܰܚܪܒܝܺܢ ܡܕ݂ܺܝܺܢܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܒܳܙܙܝܺܢ ܐܰܬܪ̈ܰܘܳܬܳܐ: ܫܳܒܶܝܢ ܘܩܳܢܶܝܢ ܠܗܘܢ ܘܡܶܕ݂ܶܡ ܠܳܐ
For to individual kings who rule every nation and tongue, their own lands do not suffice. They gather armies, join battles, ravage cities, and plunder regions; they seize and collect, and never have enough. They are vexed by works and labor, they learn war, they overturn towns, they institute hunting. They ascend, they reach the heights, then they descend to the depths, so that perhaps their greed
ܣܳܦܩܝܺܢ: ܥܳܩܪܝܺܢ ܟܰܪ̈ܟ݁ܶܐ ܘܥܳܒܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܢܰܚܫܳܐ: ܣܳܠܩܝܺܢ ܘܡܳܛܝܺܢ ܠܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܢܳܚܬܝܺܢ ܠܥܘܽܡܩܳܐ ܕܛܳܒ݂ ܬܶܣܒܰܥ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܡܰܠܝܳܐ: ܟܰܕ݂ ܢܶܣܓ݁ܺܝܐ ܥܘܽܬܪܳܐ ܚܳܪܒ݁ܳܐ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܢܶܬܝܰܬܰܪ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܳܐ ܥܰܝܦܰܬ ܥܰܝܢܳܐ
might be satisfied; but it is nowhere filled. With increasing abundance, greed grows, and with expanded riches, the proud eye grieves. Daily bread suffices for the poor; the rich man thinks of years he will not fulfill. A tattered garment suffices for the poor; but in the most delicate garments [brought] from all places, avarice remains naked. For the needy, the earth is a bed, and he is content with it; but the bed of the rich
ܕܥܰܬܝܺܪܳܐ ܠܰܝܡܳܐ: ܘܪܶܢܝܳܐ ܥܰܬܝܺܪܳܐ ܠܰܝܡܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܰܫ. ܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ ܕܪ̈ܘܽܩܥܶܐ ܡܶܣܰܬ ܡܶܣ̈ܟܺܢܶܐ: ܘܰܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ ܕܟܽܠ ܓ݁ܶܐܘܢ ܕܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܐܰܬܪ̈ܰܘܳܬܳܐ ܥܰܪܛܺܝܠܳܐܝܰܬ ܩܳܝܡܳܐ ܒܗܘܢ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܬܰܫܘܝܺܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܶܣܟܺܢܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܥܰܦ݂ܪܳܐ ܘܣܳܦ݁ܶܩ ܠܶܗ: ܘܡܰܡܫܟܒܶܗ ܕܥܰܬܝܺܪܳܐ ܥܰܪ̈ܣܳܬܳܐ ܕܟ݁ܽܠ ܓ݁ܶܐܘܢ ܘܐܰܒܘ̈ܝܺܢ ܕܟ݂ܽܠ ܓ݁ܶܢܣܺܝܢ: ܘܰܙܥܘܽܪ ܠܚܰܡܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܡܰܡܫܬܝܶܗ ܕܡܶܣܟܺܢ̈ܳܐ ܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܰܣܒܰܥ: ܘܦܳܬܶܐ ܕܥܰܬܝܺܪܳܐ ܥܰܬܝܺܩܳܐ ܘܰܠܗܝܺܩ. ܕܰܗܒ݁ܳܐ ܘܣܺܝܡܳܐ ܩܳܢܶܝܢ ܥܰܬܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܠܬܘܽܩܠܳܐ ܘܒܶܝܗ ܡܶܬܩܰܛܠܝܺܢ. ܩܰܪܝܺܕ݂ܳܐ ܫܶܢܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܟ݁ܽܠ ܪܳܚܡܰܝ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܦܳܠܶܐ ܘܢܝܺܚ
are the softest couches and all kinds of beds; and these seem little to greed. The needy drinks water, and slakes his thirst; the rich man drinks old [wine], and is afflicted with thirst. The rich man collects gold and silver, they become a stumbling block to him, and they finish him off. Sleep flees from all those who follow avarice; but the rest of the poor is gentle and most peaceful. It is in the mind of the poor man to break his bread for the needy; but the rich man thinks of consuming
ܕ݁ܢܶܩܨܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܠܰܚܡܶܗ ܠܰܣܢܝܺܩܳܐ: ܘܪܶܢܝܳܐ ܕܥܰܬܝܺܪܳܐ ܕܢܶܒܠܰܥ ܠܕܰܒܨܝܰܪ ܡܶܢܶܗ. ܛܘܽܒܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܫܡܫ ܪܰܒܘܽܬ ܟ݁ܰܪܣܳܐ: ܘܰܠܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܙܟܳܬܶܗ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܛܘܽܒܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܕ݁ܢܶܪܢܶܐ ܒܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ ܕܒܳܗ ܡܶܬܦܰܣܩܝܺܢ
those humbler than himself. Happy is he who has not served the empire of the belly, or whom greed has not overcome. Blessed is he who meditates on knowledge, by which the roots of avarice are extirpated.

ܥܰܪ̈ܦ݁ܰܝ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ܀ ܘܐܳܦ ܥܰܠ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܟܬܰܒܢ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܚܰܒ̈ܝܒܺܝܢ ܝܳܕܥܺܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܕܰܒܥܶܠܰܬ ܝܰܥܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܣܩܰܪܘ ܘܰܚܣܰܡܘ ܐ݈ܚܰܝ̈ܢ ܢܶܡܝܘܽܣܳܐ ܘܫܘܽܠܛܳܢܳܐ ܒܥܰܡܰܢ: ܟܰܕ ܫܳܠܶܡ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܰܢ ܠܗܰܠܟ̈ܳܬ݂ܰܢ. ܗܰܠܶܟܢ ܩܪܝܺܫܳܐܝܺܬ: ܘܐܶܬܪܕܝܺܢ ܩܪܝܺܫܳܐܝܺܬ. ܘܐܳܦ ܣܚܺܝܡ ܐܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܓܝܪ ܩܰܕܝܺܫܬܳܐ ܕܰܡܩܰܒܠܺܝܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ̈ܝܢ ܡܶܢܰܢ: ܠܢܶܡܣܰܬ ܣܚܳܡܳܐ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܡܶܬܟܰܬܒܳܢ ܥܠܶܝܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܰܥܓ݂ܰܠ ܡܶܫܬܟܰܚܝ ܒܙܰܒܢܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܡܫܰܐܶܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܡܰܢ ܕܕ݂ܳܚܶܠ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ܆ ܐܶܠܳܐ: ܕܡܰܢܘܽ ܩܰܫܺܝܫ ܒܰܣܚܳܡ ܐܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ܆ ܘܡܳܚܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪܘ: ܦܠܳܢ ܩܰܫܝܺܫ: ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ: ܘܳܠܶܐ ܠܡܶܬܡܳܟܘܽ ܒܪܰܫܳܐ. ܘܠܰܝܬ ܕ݁ܓ݂ܳܗܶܕ݂ ܠܥܶܒܕܰܘ̈ܗܝ ܕܦܳܪܘܽܩܳܝܐ ܕܟܰܕ ܝܳܗܶܒ ܘܳܝܳܐ ܠܣܳܦܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܠܰܦܪ̈ܝܺܫܶܐ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܰܢ: ܕܘܳܝ ܠܟܘܿܢ ܕܪܳܚܡܝܺܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܵܢ ܡܰܡܘ̈ܬܒܿܶܐ ܒܰܟ̈ܢܘܽܫ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܣܡ̈ܳܡܟܶܐ ܒܰܚܫܳܡܝ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܪܳܚܡܝܺܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܵܢ ܕ݁ܰܗܘܰܘ ܩܳܪܶܝܢ ܠܟܘܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܝܐ: ܪܰܒܝܺ ܪܰܒܝܺ. ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܢ ܫܘَܡܳܗܶܐ ܠܚܰܝܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܥܠܺܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܡܦܰܨܺܝܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܠܳܐ ܦ݁ܰܨܝܽܘ ܠܢܳܕ݁ܳܒ ܘܠܰܐܒܝܺܗܘܽ ܘܠܳܐ ܫܰܘܙܶܒ݂ܘ ܠܚܳܦܢܝ ܘܰܠܦܝܢܚܳܣ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܫܘّܡܳܗܶܐ ܥܒَܳܕ݂ܶܐ
25. Furthermore, regarding those things which we have written to you, most beloved, you know that those who hold the law and [wield] power in our people have been captured by envy and hatred, because of avarice. Our doctrine accords with our morals: we have walked manifestly, and we have been chastised manifestly. For even when men receive the holy imposition of hands from us, they attend only to the imposition; nor in our time is a man quickly found who asks: 'Who fears God?' but rather: 'Who is older in ordination?' And as soon as it was heard: 'This one is a senior'; they say to him: 'You ought to sit in the primary place.' And there is no one who reflects on the words of the Savior, cursing the scribes and Pharisees: 'Woe to you who love the first chairs in the synagogues, and the reclining places at feasts; and love to be called Rabbi, Rabbi by men.' Brothers, names neither lead to life, nor deliver from death, just as they did not save Nadab and Abihu, nor did they rescue Hophni and Phinehas; but beyond

[p. 634] {#po.0.p634}
ܛܳܒ݁ܶܐ ܢܶܬܒܥܶܝܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܥܒ̈ܺܝܕ݁ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܫܡ̈ܳܗܶܐ ܡܦܰܨܶܝܢ ܠܰܕ݂ܥܳܡܠܺܝܢ ܒܗܘܿܢ: ܘܰܫܘ̈ܳܗܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܒَܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܡܰܘܬܪܝܺܢ ܘܰܡܥܰܕ݂ܪܝܺܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕ݁ܡܶܢ ܠܥܶܠ ܟܬܰܒܢ ܠܟܘܿܢ. ܘܰܚܬܝܺܪܝܺܢ ܒܗܘܿܢ ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܢ ܒܰܫ̈ܡܳܗܶܐ ܕܰܡܩܰܒܠܺܝܢ ܠܡܶܐܣܰܪ ܒܗܘܢ ܘܠܰܡܥܰܡܳܕܘܽ ܘܰܠܡܶܬܝܰܩܳܪܘܽ: ܘܫܰܠܺܝܛ ܐܳܢܳܐ ܠܡܶܐܡܰܪ. ܘܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܫܶܠܡܰܬ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܝ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܢܒܺܝܳܐ: ܕܪܰܒ݁ܳܐ ܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܨܶܒܝܳܢ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܥܳܢܝ ܐܶܬܒ݁ܰܕ݂ܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܪܳܥܝܳܐ. ܘܬܘܽܒ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܰܪܥܰܘ ܪ̈ܳܥܰܘܳܬܳܐ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ: ܘܥܳܢܝ ܠܳܐ ܪܥܰܘ. ܘܬܘܽܒ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܐܳܘ̄ ܪܳܥܰܘܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܕܡܰܘܒܕܝܺܢ ܘܰܡܒܰܕܪܝܺܢ ܠܺܝܥܢܳܐ ܕܡܰܪܥܝܺܬܝ. ܘܬܘܽܒ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܪ̈ܳܥܰܘܳܬܳܐ: ܕܪܶܥܝܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܛܳܒܳܐ ܪܳܥܶܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܵܢ: ܘܡܺܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܡܰܘܬܪܝܺܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܵܢ ܕܳܝܫܺܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܒܪ̈ܶܓ݂ܠܰܝܟܘ̇ܢ: ܘܡܰܝܳܐ ܒܰܣܺܝܡܳܐ ܫܳܬܶܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܿܢ ܘܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܡܰܘܬܪܝܺܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܿܢ ܕܳܝܫܺܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܒܪ̈ܶܓ݂ܠܰܝܟܘܽܢ: ܘܒܰܝܢܳܬ ܙܰܥܺܝ ܕ݁ܰܕ݂ܘܳܫܳܐ ܕܪ̈ܶܓܠܰܝܟܘܽܢ ܘܐܰܫܬܺܝ ܡܳܐ ܕܠܰܚܬܳܐ ܕܐܰܘܬܰܪܬܘܽܢ. ܘܬܘܽܒ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܪ̈ܳܥܰܘܳܬܳܐ: ܕܫܰܡ̈ܢܳܬܳܐ ܕ݂ܥܳܢܳܐ ܐܳܟܠܺܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܵܢ ܘܥܰܡܪܳܐ ܠܳܒܫܺܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܵܢ: ܘܥܳܢܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܪܳܥܶܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܵܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܩܛܝܳܪܳܐ ܥܰܒܶܕܬܘܽܢ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ܀
names, good works are also required; for works without names deliver those who apply themselves to them; but names without good works help nothing and profit nothing, just as we wrote to you above. Our brothers are proud of the titles they have received, so that through them they may be able to bind, or flatter, or be honored; and I also have power. But today the word of the prophet is fulfilled: 'The great man speaks the desire of his soul.' He also said: 'My sheep are scattered, because there was no shepherd.' Again He says: 'The shepherds were feeding themselves, and were not feeding my flocks.' And again: 'O shepherds who destroy and dissipate the flock of my pasture.' To the shepherds He also said: 'You eat the good pasture, and whatever you leave you trample with your feet; you drink the sweetest water, and you muddy the rest with your feet. And my sheep have grazed on what was trampled by your feet, and have drunk the muddy water that you left.' Again He says to the shepherds: 'You eat the fat of the flock, and you cover yourselves with the wool; but you do not feed the flock, but have violently subdued it.'
ܐܽܘ̄ ܪܳܥܝܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܺܝܩܳܪܶܗ܆ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܰܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܕ݂ܳܐܶܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܥܰܒ݂ܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܕܝܺܠܳܟ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܐܶܢ ܩܳܐܶܡ ܠܡܳܪܶܗ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܩܳܐܶܡ: ܘܐܶܢ ܢܳܦܶܠ
26. O shepherd ignorant of your own dignity! Who are you, who judge another's servant? If he stands, he will stand to his master; but if he falls, he will fall to his master; nevertheless, he will stand.

ܠܡܳܪܶܗ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܢܳܦܶܠ: ܒܪܰܡ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܩܺܝܡ ܩܳܐܶܡ. ܐܶܢ ܕܶܙܕܰܕ݁ܰܩ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬ:
But if you cannot be justified, why do you multiply sins? And if you exalt yourself in your heart over me and say: 'I, a teacher and prince, preside over you'; I do not
ܡܶܬܬܪܚܰܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܪܶܥܝܳܢܳܟ݂ ܥܠܰܝ ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܡܰܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܘܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܥܠܰܝܟ: ܠܳܐ ܩܰܒܶܠܬܳܟ: ܐܳܣܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܝܿ. ܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܬܰܠܦܰܢܝ ܡܰܟ݁ܝܳܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܟܰܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܪܳܡ: ܘܓܶܝܐܳܐ ܘܡܶܬܚܰܬ݁ܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܐܰܠܦܰܢܝ: ܕ݁ܰܪܚܶܡܘ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܚܰܕ݂: ܟܰܕ݂ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬ ܣܶܢܶܐܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܪܘܺܓ݂ܙܳܐ ܡܠܶܐ܆ ܘܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܬܰܠܦܰܢܝ: ܕܐܶܢ ܥܳܩܶܠ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܕܝܺܠܳܟ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܐܒܰܥ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܬܳܒ݁ܰܥ ܕܝܺܠܳܟ ܘܢܳܣܶܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܪܶܒܝܳܬܳܐܢ ܘܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܐܰܠܦܰܢܝ: ܕܰܗܘܺܝܬ ܢܟܺܝܦ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܙܰܠܝܳܠ ܘܦܰܩܳܫ ܘܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܒܗܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܬܰܠܦܰܢܝ: ܕܲܫܒܽܘܩ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܢܰܦܝܶܠ ܒܓ݂ܰܘܶܗ ܘܰܚܢܺܝܩ܆ ܘܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܬܰܠܦܰܢܝ: ܕܐܰܪܚܶܡ ܠܡܶܣ̈ܟܺܢܶܐ: ܟܰܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܪܳܕܶܦ݂ ܡܶܣ̈ܟܺܢܶܐ ܟܢܰܘܳܬܳܟ݂܆ ܘܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܬܰܠܦܰܢܝ: ܕܰܫܒܽܘܩ ܕܰܒܠܶܒܳܟ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬ ܚܡܰܠ ܒܳܟ ܚܡܺܝܪܳܐ ܥܰܬܝܺܩܳܝܐ܆ ܘܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܬܰܠܦܰܢܝ: ܕܰܥܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܐܰܚܘܽܟ݂: ܟܰܕ݂ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ݁ ܡܫܰܓ݂ܶܫ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܣܰܓܺܝܐܳܐܢ
except you, and you burden me with chains. For how will you prescribe humility to me, who show yourself to be elated, proud, and arrogant? How will you teach me: 'Love one another,' who are full of hatred and anger? How will you hand down to me: 'If anyone takes what is yours, do not ask for it back,' who ask back what is yours, and take usury? How will you order me to remain chaste, who show yourself to be lustful and garrulous and fierce? How will you also prescribe to me to leave this world, who have fallen into it and have been suffocated? How will you say to me: 'Refresh the needy,' who pursue your poor companions? How will you also say: 'Dismiss what you reserve in your heart,' when you keep the old leaven hidden in yourself? How will you prescribe to me: 'Return to grace with your brother,' when you yourself disturb the whole world? For if I discover unbecoming fruits in you, will you say to me, when you yourself are a sinner and impious: 'Walk according to my words'? He who has taught and done, this one shall be called great; but he who has broken [a commandment], and has taught so, shall be called least. You have received money, and you have
ܐܶܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܚܙܝܺܬ ܒܳܟ ܦܺܐܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܳܐܶܝܢ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܝܳ: ܕܐܶܢ ܥܳܗܽܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܐܶܢ ܪܰܫܺܝܥ: ܒܳܬܰܪ ܡܶܠܰܝ̈ ܬܶܐ: ܕ݁ܡܰܠܶܦ ܘܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܪܰܒ݁ܺܝܐ ܡܶܬܩܪܶܐ: ܘܰܕ݂ܒܳܪܶܐ ܘܡܰܠܶܦ݂ ܒܨܝّܪܳܐ ܡܶܬܩܪܶܐ. ܟܶܣܦܳܐ ܩܰܒܶܠܬ ܘܨܰܪܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ: ܘܐܰܩܠܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܡܰܫܠܰܡ ܠܳܟ ܘܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܶܚܰܕܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ. ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܳܐ ܥܰܠܬ: ܘܠܰܕ݂ܐܳܬܶܝܢ ܠܡܶܥܰܠ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܒ݁ܶܩ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ. ܥܰܝܢܶܗ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܦܰܓܝܪܳܐ: ܗܘܰܝܬ ܠܳܟ ܣܰܡܝܳܐ: ܘܦܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܚܫܽܘܟ݂ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܒܠܰܝ ܥܰܝܢܳܐ. ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܘܰܝܬ ܠܳܟ ܣܰܡܝܳܐ: ܘܦܰܓܪܳܐ ܥܘܝܰܪܳܐ. ܗܳܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܨܒܘܽܐܳܐ ܕܣܰܡܝܳܐ ܕܰܠܣܰܡܝܳܐ ܡܕܰܒܰܪ: ܘܒܳܥܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܟܽܠܶܗ ܦ݁ܰܓܪܳܟ ܬܰܪܡܶܝܘܗ̱ܝ ܒܓܘܽܡܳܨܳܐ. ܡܶܠܚܳܐ ܟܰܕ݂ ܬܶܦܟ݁ܰܗ ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܕ݂ܝܳܐ. ܘܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܨܳܐܪ ܟܶܣܦܿܳܐ ܪܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܠܥܺܝܫܘܽܟܳܐ: ܘܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܰܡܢܰܓ݁ܶܕ݂ ܟܢܰܘܳܬܶܗ ܡܳܪܶܗ ܬܳܒ݁ܰܥ ܒܝܰܕ݂ܶܗ. ܘܪܳܥܝܳܐ ܒܘܽܪܳܐ ܥܰܝܢܶܗ ܡܶܬܥܰܘܪܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܪܳܥܶܗ ܝܳܒܶܫ. ܟܳܗܢܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪܘ: ܐܰܝܟܰܘ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ܆ ܘܐܰܚܺܝܕܰܝ̈ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܝܰܕܥܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܘܪܰܥܰܘܳܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܓܶܠܘ ܒܺܝܗ: ܘܡܶܢ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܕܐܘܿܪܺܫܠܶܡ ܢܶܦܩܰܬ ܚܰܢܦܘܽܬܳܐ ܒܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܫܰܠܺܝܛܰܝ̈ܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܥܰܡܝ ܡܟܰܥܙܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ: ܘܢܶܫ̈ܶܐ ܐܶܫܬܰܠܰܛܝ̈ ܒܶܗ. ܡܶܟܝܺܠ ܡܶܢ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܕܚܶܠܢ: ܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܠܰܢ܆ ܘܳܝ ܠܰܢ܆ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܗܘܶܢ ܕܰܒܒܰܛܠ ܢܶܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܘܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܒܚܺܝܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ̈ܝܺܢ ܡܶܢܰܢ ܒܥܰܘܠܳܐ. ܘܳܠܶܐ ܠܰܢ ܕܢܶܬܶܒ ܘܢܶܫܬܘܽܩ ܘܢܶܬܡܰܗ. ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܝܳ: ܕܬܿܳܐ ܗܘܺܝ ܥܰܡܰܝܢ ܫܰܘܬܳܦܳܐ ܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ. ܡܶܟܝܶܠ ܡܰܠܦܳܢܳܐ: ܥܠܰܝܟ ܫܳܠܡܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܚܳܕ݂ܪܺܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܝܰܡܳܐ ܘܚܰܒܫܳܐ ܕܬܶܥܒܕܘܢ ܚܰܕ݂
hidden it. The key has been handed to you, but you have closed the door; neither have you entered, nor do you allow those approaching to enter. You are the eye of the body, but you have been made blind; and the body, with the eye failing, is dark. You have been made blind, and the body is in darkness. A blind man has undertaken the care of leading the blind; and you want to precipitate the whole body into the pit. Salt, if it has become insipid, will be cast out. The servant who hid the money will be sent into darkness. The servant who has struck his fellow servants will give penalties to his master. The eye of the foolish shepherd will be blinded, and his arm will wither. The priests did not say: 'Where is the Lord?' And those holding the law did not know Him; and the shepherds have lied against Him; and from the prophets of Jerusalem pollution has gone out into all the earth. The princes of his people glean it, and women have dominated them. Since we have not feared the Lord, what will the King do to us? Woe to us! What has happened to us, because the law has been forsaken, and some of us boast in iniquity? It behooves us to sit in silence and stupor. You say to me: 'Come so that you may be a companion to us in all that I have done.' Therefore over you, O teacher! the word of the Lord is completed: 'You go around sea and dry land, to make one proselyte; and when he has been made, you make'

[p. 640] {#po.0.p640}
ܓܚܽܘܪܳܐ: ܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܗܘܳܐ ܥܳܒܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܐܢܸܬܘܽܢ ܠܶܗ ܒܪܳܗ ܕܓܺܗܰܢܳܐ. ܢܒܺܝܳܐ ܐܰܛܥܝܺ ܘܟܰܕܶܒ݂ ܒܚܰܒܪܶܗ: ܘܥܰܠ ܕܰܫܡܰܥ ܡܶܠܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܐܶܬܝܺܗܶܒ ܠܐܰܪܝܳܐ ܘܐܰܒܪܶܗ. ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܛܥܰܘ ܟܳܗܢܶܐ ܘܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܣܰܓܺܝ̈ܐܶܐ ܒܝܰܘܡܰܝ̈ ܐܳܚܳܒ: ܐܶܫܬܒܶܩܘ ܠܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ
him a son of hell. The prophet deceived his companion, and lied; but he, because he had agreed to his words, was handed over to the lion, which crushed him. When also many priests and prophets in the days of Ahab went astray, seven thousand were left to God, who did not bend their knees, and did not worship Baal (Elijah is not to be numbered among them), and they did not follow the impious and blind priests, who lead into destruction.
ܫܰܒܥܳܐ ܐܰܠܦܺܝ̈ܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܣܓ݂ܶܕ݂ܘ ܠܒܰܥܠܳܐ: ܕܐܳܦ ܠܳܐ ܐܶܠܺܝܳܐ ܪܓܺܝܫ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ: ܘܒܳܬܰܪ ܟ݁ܳܗܢܶܝ̈ܐ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܣܡ̈ܰܝܳܐ ܢܳܓܕ݁ܰܝ̈ ܠܐܰܒ݂ܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܐܶܙܰܠܘ. ܐܶܢ ܪܚܰܒܥܰܡ ܦܠܰܓ ܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܐܺܙܰܠ ܠܝ ܒܳܬܪܶܗ܆ ܚܣ ܠܝ݇. ܐܶܢ
If Rehoboam divided the kingdom, shall I follow him? Far be it! If Jeroboam left his God, shall I hold his footsteps? From these, save me, my God!
ܝܘܽܪܳܒܥܰܡ ܫܒܰܩ ܐܰܠܳܗܶܗ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܐܶܪܕܶܐ ܠܝܽ ܒܥܶܩ̈ܒܳܬܶܗ܆ ܐܰܠܳܗܝ ܦ݁ܰܨܰܢܝ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ܀ ܐܰܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܝ ܕܐܶܢܳܐ ܚܰܝܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܘܫܰܦܺܝܪ: ܘܰܓܒܳܢܝ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܰܠܫܰܡܫܳܐ ܡܫܰܚ ܕܐܰܡܠܶܟ݂ ܥܰܠ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܥܰܡܝ. ܐܶܬܛܦܰܝܣ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܰܚܪܺܝܫܳܐ ܕܚܰܝܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܰܡܠܰܟ ܠܦܺܝܢܝܺܝܣ ܒܰܪ ܐܶܠܥܳܙܳܪ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܩܝܳܡܳܐ ܕܟܳܗܢܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܘܠܰܒܢܰܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܠܥܳܠܰܡ: ܘܫܰܡܶܫ ܦܺܝܢܝܶܝܣ ܟܳܗܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܝܰܘܡܰܝ̈ ܕܰܕܰܝܳܢܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܬܠܳܬܡܳܐܐ ܘܶܫܬܺܝܢ ܘܚܰܡܶܫ ܫܢ̈ܝܺܢ. ܘܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪܟܶܢ ܩܳܡ ܥܺܠܝܽ ܒܳܬܪܶܗ. ܩܰܕܺܝܫܳܐ ܡܘܽܠܒܳܢܶܗ: ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܠܥܺܠܝܽ
27. But you will say to me: 'I am becoming and beautiful, and God chose and anointed me to rule over the sons of my people.' But be instructed, O man! [and know] that God promised by oath to Phinehas the son of Eleazar that the covenant of the priesthood would be kept by him and his sons forever; and Phinehas served in the priesthood all the days of the judges, namely, three hundred and sixty-five years; then Eli rose up after him; and when he and his sons had transgressed the law, [God] said to him through the prophet: 'Speaking I have spoken, that you and the house of your father should serve in my sight forever.' Now, however, far be this from me,
ܒܚܰܕ݂ ܢܒܺܝܳܐ: ܕܡܐܡܰܪ ܐܶܡܪܶܬ ܕܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܒܺܝܬ ܐܰܒܘܽܟ݂ ܬܫܰܡܫܘܽܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡܰܝ ܠܥܳܠܰܡ܂ ܡܶܟܝܺܠ ܚܳܣ ܠܝ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܕܰܡܚܰܩܪܳܢܰܝ̈ ܐܶܝܩܰܪ ܘܰܡܝܰܩܪܳܢܰܝ̈ ܢܶܨܛܰܥܪܘܽܢ. ܘܐܳܦ݂ ܐܝܰܣܚܶܩ ܐܰܒܘܽܢ ܨܳܒ݂ܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܰܢܒܰܪܶܟ݂ ܠܥܺܣܘܽ ܒܘܽܟܪܶܗ: ܘܝܰܥܩܘܽܒ݂ ܐܶܬܓܒܺܝ ܡܶܢ ܟܪܶܣ ܐܶܡܶܗ ܘܩܰܒܶܠ ܒܘܽܪ̈ܟܳܬܳܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܰܡܰܪ ܠܳܗ ܠܪܶܦܩܳܐ: ܕܪܰܒܳܐ ܢܶܫܬܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܠܰܙܥܘܽܪܳܐ. ܘܰܓܒܳܐ ܩܰܕܺܝܫܳܐ ܠܫܳܐܘܽܠ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ: ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܥܒܰܕ݂ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܓܒܳܐ ܠܕ݂ܰܘܝܺܕ݂ ܘܐܰܣܠܺܝܗ ܠܫܳܐܘܽܠ: ܘܰܡܕܰܒܪܺܝܢ ܘܡܰܝܬ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܢ ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܢ ܡܰܦܰܩ ܒܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܦܰܟܺܝܗܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܕܳܒܿܶܩ: ܕܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ ܠܰܡ ܕܙܰܒܢܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܐܰܩܺܝܡܰܢ ܪܺܝܫܳܐ ܠܥܰܡܶܗ ܕ݁ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܰܝܕܰܥܬܳܐ ܚܳܪܝܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܡܫܰܚܝ ܒܬܰܘܳܢܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܫܰܐܶܠ ܠܳܟ: ܐܳܘ ܣܳܦ݂ܪܳܐ ܚܰܟܺܝܡܳܐ: ܕܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܐܶܬܡܠܶܟ݂ ܡܘܽܠܟܳܢܳܐ ܕܢܶܬܡܫܰܚ ܝܶܗܘܽ ܘܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܐܶܬܳܐ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܡܫܺܝܚܘܽܬܳܐ: ܡܳܢܳܐ ܬܺܐܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ܆ ܐܶܬܦܩܶܕ݂ ܐܶܠܺܝܫܳܐ ܒܛܘܽܪܳܐ ܕܚܘܽܪܶܒ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܕܙܶܠ ܘܰܡܫܘܽܚ ܠܝܶܗܘܽ ܕܢܰܡܠܶܟ݂ ܥܰܠ ܐܝܺܣܪܳܝܶܠ
says the Lord; but those who glorify me I will glorify; and those who despise me shall be held in contempt. Isaac also, our father, had wished to bless Esau, his firstborn; but Jacob, chosen from his mother's womb, received the blessing, just as God spoke to Rebecca: The elder shall serve the younger. Saul also was chosen by the Holy One to become king; but when he did not execute the will of God, [God] chose David and rejected Saul. Nevertheless, brothers, they bring us a painted, foolish, and inept response [saying]: Thus God appointed us over His people in adverse times, just as He did Jehu, who received his anointing in a chamber. But if someone should ask you, O wise scribe! when the anointing of Jehu was promised, and when he was gifted with the anointing, what will you say to him? [God] commanded Elijah on Mount Horeb, saying: Go and anoint Jehu, that he may reign over Israel, that he may destroy the house of Ahab. This command, therefore, Elijah received, and he ministered for many years, until he was taken up. After him, however, [arose] Elisha. And when the time had arrived [for Jehu to reign], and the measure of the iniquities of the house of Ahab was overflowing, Elisha sent one of the sons of the prophets, who went and anointed Jehu, just as he


[p. 641] {#po.0.p641}


[p. 642] {#po.0.p642}
ܘܢܰܘܒܶܝܕ݂ ܠܒܰܝܝܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܐܰܚܺܝܒ. ܐܶܬܦܣܶܝܕ݂ ܐܶܠܺܐ ܘܫܰܡܫ ܫܫ̈ܰܬܐ ܣܰܔ̈ܺܐܳܬܳܐ ܥܰܕ݂ ܡܶܣܬܰܠܰܩ. ܘܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܪܶܗ ܐܶܠܫܫ̈ܰܥ. ܘܟܰܝܕ݂ ܡܛܳܝܐ ܙܰܒܪܶܚܗ ܕܝܗܘ ܘܦܶܦܥܰܬ ܟܣܶܠܬܳܐ ܕܰܚ݁ܛܺܝܗܶܐ ܕܒܰܚܬܶܗ ܕܐܳܚܺܒ: ܗܳܚܕ݁ܶܚܢ ܫܰܕ݁ܰܪ ܐܰܠܚܫܰܥ ܠܚܰܢܕ ܡܶܢ ܒܚܢܰܚܝ̈ ܢܝܟܰܚܢܶܚܐ: ܘܐܶܙܰܠ ܘܡܰܒܫܚܶܶܗ ܐܰܝ ܕܐ݂ܶܦܩܶܕ݂. ܘܐܲ ܕܝܢ ܠܚܪܗܬ ܡܕܰܡܶܝܢ ܠܳܗ ܠܰܨܒܝܘܽܬܳܐ: ܡܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܟܰܢܳܝܐ ܐܶܬܦܰܩܰܝܕ݂ ܥܰܠ ܟܳܝܘܢܳܐ ܕܰܢܩܘܽܡ ܒܥܰܡܳܝܐ: ܕܡܐ ܕܩܺܝܡ ܢܰܚܘܒܶܕ݂ ܠܟܠ ܗܘܿܢ ܐܰܚܰܚܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܘܢܶܐܣܘܽܪ ܘܰܢܫܰܧܶܒܕ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܚܪܰܒ݂ ܚܳܗܘܽ ܘܐܰܘܒ݁ܶܝܕ݂ ܠܒܰܫܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܐܳܚܳܒ. ܗܳܢܳܐ ܡܰܦ݁ܰܩ ܒܪܘܽܚܳܝܐ ܠܕ݂ܰܐܙܰܒ݁ܺܝܠ ܕܳܡܶܝܐ: ܕܟ݂ܰܝܕ݂ ܚܝܪܳ ܠܗܘ ܕܐܰܡܠܶܟ ܘܐܳܬܶܐ ܐܶܨܛܰܒܬܰܬ ܘܐܰܕܝܚܺܩܰܬ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܢ ܦ݁ܰܝܘܬܳܐ ܘܐܶܡܪܰܐ ܠܶܗ: ݁ܬܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܫܠܺܝܡ ܙܰܡܚܪܝܺ̈ ܩܶܛܶܠ ܡܳܝܪܶܗ. ܘܡܰܝܦ݁ܰܚܩ ܒܝܪܘܽܚܳܶܐ ܚܰܝܒܳܝܗ:
had been commanded. If, however, we were to equate our affairs with the affairs of Jehu in this way, would it then have been prescribed to the priest to preside over the people in such a way that, having obtained the prefecture, he would destroy, bind, and seduce all his brothers, just as Jehu devastated and destroyed the house of Ahab? A response of this kind is similar to that which Jezebel brought, who, when she saw Jehu, having obtained the kingdom, approaching, adorned herself, and looking at him through the window, said to him: Come in peace, Zimri, murderer of your master. But her own response condemned her; for Jehu killed her too, and tore her apart, and threw her to the dogs.

ܘܐܳܦ ܠܳܗ ܩܰܬܛܠܳܗ ܚܳܗܘܽ ܘܦܰܫܚܺܝܗܘ ܘܰܢܕ݂ܳܗ ܠܟܰܠܒܶܐ܀ ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܢ ܟܝܪܕܶܣ ܐܶܡܶܗ ܐܶܬܔܓܒܥ̈ ܐܰܟ ܝܰܥ ܘܽܒ ܢܺܝܐܡܪܘܽܢ ܠܢ ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܪܒ݁ܥܰܝܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܐܶܬܩܰܕܰܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܶܪܰܡܐ܆ ܘܐܶܢ ܐܶܬܪܫ݁ܶܡ ܠܡܰܠܟ݁ܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܩܝܪܝܺ ܒܪܳܐ ܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܫܠܝܡܘ̇ܢ܆ ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܢ ܩܕܳܡ ܒܛܚܰܢܘܽܬ݂ܳܗ ܐܶܬܔܝ ܒܝ ܐܰܝܟ ܚܘܽܫ̈ܺܚܐܵ ܘܐܶܢ ܒܢܳܐ ܗܰܝܟܠܳܐ ܐܰܝ ܟܘܽܪܶܦ.܆ ܘܐܶܬܛܦܝܵܣ ܐܰܘ ܒܰܚܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܝܫܳܚܐ܆ ܕܐܵܗܪܘܽܢ ܠܳܐ ܫܰܝܒܰܝܚ ܢܰܗ ܥܶܚܗ ܕܢܶܝܗܘܶܐ ܪܰܒ ܟ ܘܽܡܪܶܐ. ܘܐܳܦ ܡܝܘܽܩܶܝܐ ܟ݁ܰܝܕ݂ ܨܒܳܐ ܡܺܝܪܶܗ ܕܢܶܥܒܕ݂ܝܽܘܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܠܳܗ ܠܟܶܚܡܘܿܢ ܘܐܶܫܶܚܐ ܠܰܟ݁ܢܰܝܚ ܥܰܘܶܒܗ: ܙܰܒܥ̈ܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܣܰܔܫ̈ܺܝܐܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܐܶܝܬܙܶܠ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܚܐ ܕܡܶܶܢ ܐܘ̈ܠܨܳܢܳܝܚܐ ܪܰܒ݁ܳܚܐ ܫܰܚܕ݂ܪܶܗ ܠܡܶܨܪܶܝܢ ܘܰܥܒܰܝܕ݂ ܒܐܝܺܕܶܗ ܢܶܣܶܝܐ ܘܐܳܬܘ̈ܳܬܳܐ܀
28. And if [someone] was chosen from his mother's womb, like Jacob, they will say to us; or if he was sanctified from the womb, like Jeremiah? or even if he was predestined to the kingdom like Solomon, and called the son of God? or finally, before he was conceived, was chosen like Josiah? or is he to rebuild the temple, like Cyrus? Know, however, O man! that Aaron did not glorify himself to become high priest; Moses also, when his Lord wanted to make him a god to Pharaoh and a prince to the sons of his people, refused once and again, until [the Lord] sent him from great distress into Egypt, and through him performed signs and wonders.

[p. 646] {#po.0.p646}
ܐܰܘ ܒܪܰܘܡܳܝܐ ܕܩܰܘܡܬܶܗ ܢܚܘܽܪ ܐܰܟ ܕ݁ܰܒ݂ܫܺܝܐܘܳܠ: ܐܰܘ ܒܚܶܝܙܘܶܗ ܕܫܰܦܺܝܪ ܐܰܟ ܕܐܶܠܚܺܝܒ: ܐܰܘ ܒܝܰܬܺܝܪܬܳܐ ܫܘܽܦܪܶܗ ܐܰܟ ܕܐܰܒܺܫܠܘܽܡ: ܠܳ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܡܳܪܳܐ ܒܚܶܙܘܳܐ ܘܐܳܦ݂ ܠܳܐ ܒܪܳܡܶܐ ܘܰܚܬܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ: ܫܡܘܺܐܶܝܠ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܒܳܚܰܪ ܠܶܒܳܐ: ܘܼܒܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܚܳܙܶܐ ܒܥܰܝܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ. ܘܰܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܰܓܒܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܣܰܟ̈ܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕ݁ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܕܢܰܒܗܶܬ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܠܚܰܟܺܝܡܶܐ: ܘܰܓܒܳܐ ܟܪ̈ܝܳܗܶܐ ܕܢܰܒܗܶܬ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܠܚܰܝܠܬ݁ܳܢܶܐ: ܘܰܓܒܳܐ ܚܰܣܝܽܪ̈ܰܝ ܛܘܽܗܡܳܐ ܘܰܒܨܝܰܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܡܰܣ̈ܠܰܚܐ ܘܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܰܢܒܰܛܶܠ ܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܐܺܝܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܫܬ݁ܰܒ݁ܗܰܪ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܒܣܰܪ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܕ݂ܡܶܢܶܗ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܘܐܳܦ ܐܶܪܰܡܝܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܫܬܰܒܗܰܪ ܚܰܝܠܬ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܒܰܚܰܝܠܶܗ ܘܥܰܬܝܺܪܳܐ ܒܥܘܽܬܪܶܗ ܘܓܰܢ̱ܒܳܪܳܐ ܒܓܰܢ̱ܒܳܪܘܳܬܶܗ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܢ ܕܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܒ݂ܗܰܪ ܒ݁ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܢܶܫܬܰܒܗܰܪ. ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܝܐ ܒܪܝܺܬ݁ܶܗ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܩܕ݂ܳܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܘܒܪ ܚܺܐܪܶܐ ܘܥܰܬܝܺܪܳܐ ܘܡܶܣܟܺܢܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܟܽܠ ܕܠܶܗ ܦܳܠܚܺܝܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܫܘܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ. ܘܐܶܢ ܒܣܘܽܓܐܳܐ ܕܡܰܡܠ̱ܠܳܐ ܘܒܚܺܕ݂ܰܥܬܳܐ ܝܰܬܝܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ
29. Or shall we look at the eminence of stature, like Saul's; or the illustrious appearance, like Eliab's; or the exceptional beauty, like Absalom's? But the Lord is not delighted by appearance, nor does He love the proud or the boastful. For Samuel says: The Lord looks at the heart, but man sees with his eyes. And the Apostle says: God chose the foolish of the world, that through them He might confound the wise; He chose the weak, that through them He might confound the strong; the ignoble, and the least, and the despised, and those who are nothing, He chose, that He might destroy those who are something, so that no flesh may boast in the sight of God, from whom you are. Jeremiah also: Let not the strong man boast in his strength, nor the rich man in his riches, nor the robust man in his vigor; but let him who boasts, boast in the Lord. For all men are creatures of God, nor is there before Him servant or free, nor rich or needy, but all who serve Him are equal before Him. Even if men boast in the richness of their speech or the sublimity of their knowledge, in this too they do not prevail. For thus it is written: He will not hear the abundance of words, nor shall a wordy man be justified by his speeches. Again it is written: He takes away speech from the truthful, and removes the sense of the elders.
ܢܶܫܬܰܒܗܪܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟܚܝܺܢ ܙܳܟܶܝܢ ܒܗܳܕܶܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܟܬܝܺܒ: ܕܰܒܣܘܺܓ݁ܐܳܐ ܕܡܶܠܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܥܳܢܶܐ: ܐܳܦ ܠܳܐ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܡܰܠܳܠܳܐ ܒܦܶܬܓ݂ܳܡܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܙܕܰܕܰܩ. ܘܬܘܒ ܟܬܝܺܒ: ܕܡܰܥܒܰܪ ܡܰܡܠ̱ܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܗܰܝ̈ܡܢܶܐ ܘܛܰܥܡܳܐ ܕܣܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܫܳܩܶܠ: ܥܰܡ ܣܰܓ̈ܺܝܐܳܬܳܐ ܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ̈ܳܢ܀

ܰܡ ܕ̈ܝܢ ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܪܗܰܛܺܘ ܒܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܘܰܥܡܰܠܘ ܒܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܘܕܰܥܟܶܟܘ ܒܧܺܫܬܳܐ ܘܐܰܥܩܰܪܘ ܒܥܶܠܕܒܺܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܫܰܝܢܘ ܡܰܪ̈ܝܺܪܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܠܳܐ ܡܶܙܕ݂ܟܶܐ ܩܘܽܫܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܘܠܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܝܒܳܐ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܽܫܥܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܐܰܩ ܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܚܶܪܝܳܫܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܟܰܕ݁ܰܒ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕܰܓ݁ܳܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܫܳܠܶܡ ܟܺܐܢܳܐ ܠܥܰܘܳܠܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܙܰܕ݂ܝܺܩܳܐ ܠܪܰܫܺܝܥܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܛܳܒ݁ܳܐ ܠܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܰܠܝܳܐ ܠܡܰܪܝܺܪܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܶܫܘܽܟ݁ܳܐ ܠܢܰܗܝܳܪܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܙܰܗܪܳܐ ܠܥܰܡܛܳܢܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܦܰܟܺܝܗܳܐ ܠܰܡܠܺܝܚܳܐ. ܘܠܳܐ ܚܡܺܝܪܳܐ ܥܰܬܝܺܩܳܐ ܠܰܓܒܺܝܠܬܳܐ ܚܕ݂ܰܬܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܢܘܽܪܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܠܦܳܓܘܽܫܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܗܰܝܡ̈ܢܶܐ ܠܰܡܒܰܙܚܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܛܺܝܪ̈ܰܝ ܬܳܓ݁ܳܐ ܠܰܐܣܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܝܰܡܺܝܢܳܐ ܠܰܒ݁ܢܰܝ ܣܶܡܳܠܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܰܒ݁ܢܰܝ ܓ݁ܺܗܰܢܳܐ ܘܐܳܦ݂ܠܳܐ ܕܶܚܠܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܡܰܓ݂ܢܝܳܢ ܡܰܪܥܺܝܬܶܗ: ܘܐܳܦ݂ܠܳܐ ܥܺܕܬܳܗ ܕܩܰܕܺܝܫܳܐ ܠܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܒܺܝܫܳܐ. ܠܳܐ ܡܶܣܬ݁ܰܬܰܪ ܥܰܘܠܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܛܰܫܶܐ ܕܰܓܳܠܘܽܬܳܐ: ܡܢ ܓܶܝܪ ܕܕܳܒܶܐ ܕܢܶܝܪܗܰܛ ܘܢܶܥܡܰܠ ܕ݁ܚܰܝܪܘܽܬ ܦܳܪܘܽܩܰܢ: ܕܛܘܽܒܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܠܥܳܒܽܕ݂ܰܝ ܫܠܳܡܳܐ: ܕܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܢܶܬܩܪܘܽܢ܂ ܡܰܢܘܽ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܳܓܶܓ ܕ݁ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܪܳܐ ܠܰܐܒܳܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܐܰܚܳܐ ܠܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ܀
30. Nevertheless, brothers, pursue peace, devote labor to quiet; extinguish malice, remove enmities, mitigate the exasperated; for iniquity will not overcome equity, nor will malice conquer justice, nor will peace be restrained by sedition, nor will a lie argue against the truth of the false; nor can the just consent with the perverse, nor the upright man with the malignant, nor the good with the iniquitous, nor the sweet with the bitter, darkness with light, clarity with gloom, nor the salty with the insipid, nor the old leaven with the new dough, nor fire with water, nor the sons of peace with the seditious, or the faithful with the mockers, nor those who are crowned with a diadem with those who are held in chains, nor the sons of the right hand with those who are on the left, nor the sons of the kingdom with the sons of Gehenna, nor those who fear God with those who disturb His pasture with sedition, nor the church of the Holy One with the doctrines of the malignant. Iniquity will not be hidden, nor will a lie be concealed; and whoever wishes to run, and to apply himself to peace and quiet, will receive the blessedness which our Savior has granted: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the sons of God. Who would not wish to become a son of the Father who is in heaven and a brother of the King Christ?

ܚܙܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܢ ܟܡܐ ܫܳܘܶܝܢ ܠܕ݂ܘܰܟ݁ܪܳܢܳܐ
31. See, however, brothers, how those who labor for the quiet and peace of the people are worthy of memory. What did the
ܕܥܰܡܳܝܐ. ܡܳܢܳܝܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܚܰܝܳܒ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܦܳܪܘܺܩܰܢ ܠܡܰܘܬܳܐ܆ ܘܡܳܢܳܝܐ ܚܰܙܶܦ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܫܝܘܽܠ܆ ܕܟܰܝܕ݂ ܚܳܝܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܝܬ ܚܠܳܦ ܡܰܪ̈ܝܺܕܶܐ ܘܫܰܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܥܰܡ ܐܰܒܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܘܥܰܠ ܠܰܫܝܘܽܠ ܘܐܰܦܶܩ ܚܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܝܗ: ܘܥܰܡ ܒ݁ܺܝܫܳܝܐ ܐܶܬܟܰܬܰܫ ܘܰܙܟܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܘܕܳܫܶܗ ܘܰܐܪܰܥ ܕܘܽܪ̈ܟ݁ܳܬ݂ܶܗ ܘܚܰܠܶܨ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܶܗ: ܬܰܒܰܪ ܬܰܪ̈ܥܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܓܰܕܶܡ ܡܘܽܟ݁ܠܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ: ܘܩܘܽܒܳܝܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܟܩܰܠ ܘܣܳܡ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܪܺܝܫܶܗ: ܚܰܬܶܡ ܢܰܦ݁ܫܳܬܰܢ ܒܰܕܡܳܐ ܕܢܰܦܫܶܗ: ܫܪܳܐ ܐܰܣܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܓܘܰܒܳܐ ܚܒܺܝܫܳܐ: ܬ݁ܪܰܥ ܣܝܳܓܳܝܐ ܘܰܦܨܰܡܳܝܐ ܕܚܰܪܒܳܐ ܘܰܢܩܰܠ ܠܰܘܛܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܩܰܒܥܳܗ ܒܰܙܩܺܝܦܶܗ: ܟܰܢܶܫ ܡܒܰܕ݁ܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܫܰܝܢ ܡܰܪ̈ܚܺܝܩܶܐ: ܣܰܒܰܥ ܩܰܦ݁ܺܝ̈ܢܶܐ ܘܐܰܫܩܝܺ ܠܕ݂ܰܨܗܶܝܢ: ܦܰܬܰܚ ܥܘܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܐܰܚܠܶܡ ܟܪ̈ܝܳܗܶܐ: ܦܫܰܛ ܟܦܺܝܦܶܐ ܘܗܰܠܶܟ݂ ܚܓܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ܆ ܢܰܛܶܠ ܟܺܐܒ݁ܰܝܳܢ ܘܐܰܚܠܶܡ ܡܰܚܘܳܬܰܢ ܘܐܣܝܺ ܟܪ̈ܝܳܗܘܳܬܰܢ: ܘܩܰܪܶܒ݂ ܪܰܚܺܝܩܘܽܬܰܢ ܘܟܰܢܶܫ ܡܒܰܕܪܘܽܬܰܢ ܘܥܰܒܕ݂ܰܢ ܒܰܢܰܝ ܕܳܝܪܶܗ: ܐܰܥܬܪܰܢ ܒܶܡܣܟܺܢܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܒܰܟܪܝܺܗܘܽܬܶܗ ܐܰܚܠܡܰܢ: ܐܰܣܝܰܢ ܒܰܙܩܺܝܦܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܰܒܐܘܽܠܨܳܢܰܘ̈ܗܝ ܪܰܘܚܰܢ: ܘܰܚܠܳܦ ܕܗܳܠܶܝܢ
Savior owe to death? or what was it that He had borrowed from hell? who, while He lived, died for the rebellious, and reconciled them with His Father. He penetrated into hell, and led out its captives; He wrestled with the malignant, and overcame and trampled him, disturbed his tracks, plundered his possessions, tore down the gates, and broke the bars; and taking his thorns, He placed them upon His own head; He marked our souls with His own blood; He freed the bound from the closed pit; He [broke through] the hedge, broke the point of the sword, took away the curse, and affixed it to His cross. He gathered the dispersed, and pacified the disobedient. He satisfied the hungry, and gave drink to the thirsty; He opened the eyes of the blind, healed the languishing, raised up the bent, and made the lame walk; He took away our diseases, cured our wounds, and healed our sickness; He brought back our departure, and gathered our dispersion, and made us sons of His mansion. By His poverty He enriched us, by His own languor He refreshed us, by His crucifixion He healed us, and by His torments He recreated us. And because He suffered all these things for us, He received from the Father
ܐܰܩܒܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܒܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܫܡܳܝܐ ܕܰܡܚܰܝܬܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܟܠ ܫܡܳܗܺܝܢ: ܕܒܶܗ ܒܰܫܡܳܝܐ ܕܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܬܶܟܘܰܦ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܒܪܽܘܟ ܠܳܐ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܕܒܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܦ݂ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܝܐ: ܘܟܰܝܕ݂ ܟ݁ܳܪܥܺܝܢ ܘܣܳܓܕܝܺܢ ܢܺܐܡܪܘܽܢ ܕܡܳܪܝܰܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܝܽܚܳܐ ܠܫܘܽܒܚܶܗ ܕ݁ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܰܒܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܕܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܘܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܡܺܝ̈ܬܶܐ ܘܰܠܚܰ̈ܝܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܒܰܐܘܢܓܶܠܝܳܢܶܗ: ܕܐܰܒܳܐ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܠܳܐ ܕܳܐܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܕܺܝܢܳܐ ܠܰܒܪܶܗ ܢܶܬܠܶܝܘܗ̱ܝ: ܐܰܓܪܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܥܰܡܠܳܗ ܕܦܳܪܘܽܩܰܝܢ ܗܳܢܰܘ: ܫܡܳܝܐ ܪܰܒܳܐ ܘܰܡܚܰܬܪܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܕܫܰܝܢ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܡܰܪܝܺܕ݂ܳܐ ܘܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܡܶܫܬܰܘܬܦܝܺܢ ܥܡܶܗ ܘܥܳܒܕ݁ܝܺܢ ܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܘܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܐܰܚܰܘ̈ܗܝ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܠܳܗ ܘܰܒܢ̈ܰܝܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܝܳܪܬܝܺܢ ܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܰܡܫܰܡܫܝܺܢ ܘܡܶܫܬܰܡܫܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܠܺܝܚܺܝܪ̈ܰܝ ܡܺܝܬܳܝܶܐ ܗܳܢܘܽܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܳܣܡܝܢܳܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܛܳܢܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܠܳܐܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܪܳܡܣܝܢ: ܘܕܳܝܪܺܝܢ ܒܟܰܛܳܫܶܐ ܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܬܳܝܒܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܺܛܳܗܶܐ܀
the name which is above every name, that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, not only of those on earth but also of those in heaven, and falling down and adoring, they may say that Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God His Father. And He was constituted judge and Lord of the dead and the living, just as He says in His Gospel: The Father will judge no one, but will give all judgment to His Son. For this is the reward which the Savior took for His labor; a great and more excellent name, because He calmed the region agitated by rebellion. And those who have come to the fellowship of His labor, and have devoted themselves to quiet and peace, will become His brothers and sons of God; they will inherit the kingdom, and they will minister, and it will be ministered to them by the Angels of heaven, who do not envy, nor are jealous, nor grow weary, nor sleep, and rejoice over sinners when they repent of their sins.


[p. 651] {#po.0.p651}


[p. 652] {#po.0.p652}
ܚܰܒܺܝܒܰܝ̈ ܟܬܳܒܰܘ̈ܗܝ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܶܣܬܰܬ ܕ݁ܢܺܐܠܰܦ ܕܢܶܩܪܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܦ݂ ܕܢܶܥܒܺܕ݂. ܘܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܙܝܳܐ ܠܰܢ ܨܒܘܽܬܳܐ: ܕ݁ܰܡܳܐ ܕܒܰܒܬܳܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܚܶܪܝܳܢܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܨܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܩܰܒܠܳܐ ܘܒܳܥܘܽܬܳܗ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܡܥܳܐ ܘܩܘܽܪܒܳܢܶܗ ܡܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬ݂ܡܰܠܶܐ ܘܙܶܕ̈ܩܳܬ݂ܶܗ
32. Beloved, to learn and read the scriptures of God is not enough, but one must put them into effect. And so it seems to us, if anyone is involved in insults and contention, that neither is his prayer accepted, nor his supplication heard, nor his gift taken from the earth, and alms profit nothing for the remission of sins; for as often as tranquility and peace are not found, the door is open to the malignant; [where] correction and discipline [are lacking], there is no judgment
ܕ݁ܰܠܚܘܽܣܝܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܘܬܪܳܢ. ܕܰܐܝܟܳܐ ܕܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܠܰܝܬ: ܦܬܝܺܝܚ ܬܰܪܥܳܐ ܠܒܝܺܫ̈ܳܝܐ: ܟܐܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܡܰܪܕܘܳܬܳܐ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܕܝܳܢܳܐ
nor inquiry. The wheat is confused
ܙܳܕܶܩ: ܝܳܥܶܝܢ ܟܘܽܒܶܐ: ܣܳܓ݂ܶܝܢ ܟܳܓܘܽܪ̈ܶܐ: ܣܳܓ݂ܶܝܢ ܡܡܰܚ̈ܩܳܢܶܐ. ܡܶܬܝܰܬܪܝܺܢ ܡܒܰܙܚܳܢ̈ܶܐ: ܠܰܝܬ ܡܰܟܣܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܰܝܬ ܟܘܽܘܳܢܳܐ ܠܰܝܬ ܛܰܥܡܳܐ: ܦܰܟܚܝܳܐ ܡܶܠܚܳܐ: ܚܫܘܽܟܳܐ ܥܰܝܢܳܐ: ܥܰܡܘܽܛ ܦܰܓܪܳܐ: ܫܩܝܼܠܳܐ ܬܶܐܓܘܽܪܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܠܰܕ݂ܥܳܐܶܠ ܘܢܳܦܶܩ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦ݁ܺܐܪܶܐ ܘܰܡܘܠܶܕ݂ ܚܶܪܝܳܢܳܐ. ܗܳܫܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܶܬܝܰܕ݂ܥܝܺܢ ܢܰܨܝܺܚܶܐ ܘܡܶܬܦܰܪܫܝܺܢ ܟܰܫܝܽܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܟܽܠ ܚܠܺܝܨܳܐ ܡܶܬܒܰܩܶܐ: ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܪܳܗܛܝܺܢ ܒ݁ܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܘܥܳܡܠܝܺܢ ܒܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܐܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܩܰܝܳܡ܂ ܘܦܘܽܪܥܳܢܳܐ ܣܰܓܝܳܐ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕ݂ܩܳܝܡܝܳܢ ܒܬܘܽܪܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܣܳܝܓܝܺܢ ܣܝܳܓܳܐ: ܘܝܳܗܒܝܺܢ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܠܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܐܰܦܰܝ̈ ܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ:
with tares mixed in; thorns grow, disturbers multiply, mockers prevail, rebuke, amendment, and prudence fail. The salt has become insipid, the eye darkened, the body covered in darkness. Trade is taken away; for the one entering and exiting there is no peace. Such are the fruits that contention bears. Now, however, the illustrious become known, the diligent are discerned, and all the strenuous are tested; [for those] who pursue peace and devote themselves to tranquility, there is a firm reward and ample remuneration. These are they who stand in the breach, and draw up the hedge; who deliver themselves to labor for the people, and are marked with good memory along with the illustrious and diligent servants.


[p. 653] {#po.0.p653}


[p. 654] {#po.0.p654}
ܘܡܶܬܪܰܟܡܝܺܢ ܒܕܘܽܟ݁ܪܳܢܳܐ ܛܳܒܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܢܰܨܝܺܚܶܐ ܘܒܳܡܠܶܐ ܟܰܫܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ܀ ܒܕܳܪ ܘܕܳܪ ܚܰܒܺܝܒܰܝ̈ ܘܒ݁ܰܙܒ݂ܰܢ ܘܙܒܰܢ ܐܰܟܡܳܐ ܕܰܦ݁ܰܫ ܠܛܰܝܒ݁ܽܘܬܶܗ ܥܳܒܘܽܪܰܢ ܐܰܘܪܶܒ ܙܥܘܽܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܦܰܚܶܬ ܪܳܡܶܐ: ܘܐܰܪܚܺܡ ܡܰܟ݁ܺܝܟܶܐ ܘܡܰܟ݁ܶܟ ܠܓܰܝܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܘܡܰܣܟ݁ܶܢ ܠܥܰܬܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܥܰܬܰܪ ܠܠܶܡܣ̈ܟܺܢܐ: ܘܫܰܦܶܠ ܚܰܫ̈ܠܬ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܘܚܰܫܶܠ ܡܚ̈ܚܺܝܠܶܐ: ܘܰܗܓܰܡ ܓܰܢ̱ܒܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܥܰܕܰܪ ܒܨܝܳܪ̈ܐ. ܐܰܪܚܰܡ ܠܫܶܬ ܙܥܘܽܪܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܩܳܐܶܝܢ ܒܘܽܟܪܳܐ: ܘܰܠܢܘܽܚ ܚܠܦ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܐܰܒܳܐ
33. In all generations, beloved, and in every time, our good creator, as it pleased Him, magnified the little ones and despised the haughty; He exalted the humble and humbled the proud, reduced the rich to poverty, but lifted up the poor, depressed the powerful and strengthened the weak, threw down the strong and confirmed the more tenuous. He exalted Seth, younger in age, in the place of Cain the elder, similarly Noah in the place of Adam, the author of the second world, and Isaac in the place of Ishmael, and Jacob for Esau, Joseph for Reuben, Ephraim in the place of Manasseh,
ܕ݁ܥܰܡ̈ܡܶܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܥܰܡܳܐ: ܘܰܐܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܕܰܐܩܺܝܡ ܐܝܰܫܡܳܥܶܝܠ ܚܠܳܦ ܥܳܣܘܽ: ܘܰܠܝܰܥܩܘܽܒ ܚܠܳܦ ܥܳܣܘܽ: ܘܰܠܝܰܘܣܶܦ ܚܠܳܦ ܪܘܽܒܶܝܠ: ܘܠܰܐܶܦܪܶܝܡ ܚܠܳܦ ܡܢܰܫܶܐ: ܘܠܶܐܠܺܝܥܳܙܳܪ ܘܠܐܝܺܬ݁ܳܡܳܪ ܚܠܳܦ ܢܳܕܳܒ݂ ܘܐܰܒܺܝܗܘܽ: ܘܰܠܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܘܰܠܟܳܠܳܒ ܚܠܳܦ ܥܶܣܪܳܐ ܓܳܫ̈ܘܽܫܝܺܢ ܚܰܒܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܘܠܰܫܡܘܺܐܺܝܠ ܚܠܳܦ ܥܶܠܺܝ: ܘܰܠܕ݂ܰܘܺܝܕ݂ ܚܠܳܦ ܫܳܐܘܽܠ: ܘܠܰܫܠܺܝܡܘܽܢ ܚܠܳܦ ܐܰܕܘܳܢܝܳܐ: ܘܰܠܝܳܪܳܒܥܰܡ ܚܠܳܦ ܪܚܰܒܥܰܡ: ܘܰܠܝܶܗܘܽ ܚܠܳܦ ܐܳܚܳܒ݂: ܘܰܠܡܘܽܪܕܟ݁ܰܝ ܚܠܳܦ ܗܳܡܳܢ: ܘܰܠܕ݂ܳܢܺܝܐܶܝܠ ܘܠܰܐܰܚܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܚܠܳܦ ܚܰܟܺܝܡܶܐ ܕܒܳܒܶܠ:
Eleazar and Ithamar for Nadab and Abihu, Joshua and Caleb for the ten other explorers their companions, Samuel in the place of Eli, David for Saul, Solomon for Adonijah, Jeroboam for Rehoboam, Jehu in the place of Ahab, Mordecai in the place of Haman, Daniel and his brothers in the place of the wise men of Babylon, and finally the nations in the place of the people. Similarly, He also exalted women: Sarah over Hagar, the mother of the firstborn, Rachel for Leah, Hannah for Peninnah, Esther in the place of Vashti. To women also, prophecy and judgment were sometimes handed down, as it pleased Him who lifts up the humble. For there existed Miriam the prophetess, and Anna the prophetess,


[p. 655] {#po.0.p655}


[p. 656] {#po.0.p656}
ܐܳܦܶܢ ܚܰܪܶܡ ܠܣܳܪܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܗܳܓ݂ܳܪ ܝܳܠܕ݂ܰܬ ܒܘܽܟܪܳܐ: ܘܰܠܪܳܚܶܠ ܚܠܳܦ ܠܺܝܐ: ܘܰܠܚܰܢܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܦܰܢܳܢܶܐ: ܘܠܶܐܶܣܬܝܺܪ ܚܠܳܦ ܘܰܫܬܝܺ. ܘܐܳܦ ܢܒܺܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܕܺܝܢܳܐ ܐܶܫܬܠܶܡ ܠܢܶܫ̈ܶܐ ܒܰܙܒܰܢ ܙܒܰܢ ܕܰܨܒܳܐ ܡܪܝܳܐ ܡܰܟܟ݁ܳܢܳܐ: ܡܰܪܝܰܡ ܢܒܺܝܬܳܐ ܘܚܰܢܳܐ ܢܒܺܝܬܳܐ ܚܘܽܠܕܝܺ ܢܒܺܝܬܳܐ ܐܶܠܝܰܫܒܳܥ ܢܒܺܝܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܪܝܰܡ ܢܒܺܝܬܳܐ ܝܳܠܕ݂ܰܬ ܢܒܺܝܚܳܝܐ ܪܰܒܳܐ: ܘܰܕܒܝܘܽܪܳܐ ܢܒܺܝܬܳܐ ܕܳܢܰܬ ܠܐܝܺܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܒܝܰܘܡ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܕܒܳܪܳܩ ܒܰܪ ܐܰܒܝܺܢܥܳܡ
and Huldah the prophetess, and Elizabeth the prophetess, and Mary the prophetess, the Mother of the great Prophet. Deborah also, the prophetess, judged Israel, in the days of Barak the son of Abinoam, the king. Nor shall anyone rebuke the will of our good God, for no one will ever scrutinize His judgments, His ways cannot be inquired into, His judgments are infinite, and His thought is immense.
ܡܰܠܟܳܐ. ܘܠܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܪܳܫܶܐ ܕܶܒܚܳܢܶܗ ܕܛܳܒܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܰܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܳܫ ܕܝܳܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ: ܘܐܘܰܪ̈ܚܳܬ݂ܶܗ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܥܰܩ̈ܒܳܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܣܬ݁ܰܝܟܝܺܢ ܕܝܳܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܡܰܫܚܳܐ ܬܰܪܥܝܺܬܶܗ܀ ܪܰܘܪܰܒܝܺܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܥܒܳܕ݂ܰܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܥܰܡܺܝܩܺܝܢ ܘܰܐܡܺܝܪ̈ܳܢ ܡܰܚܫ̈ܒܳܬܶܗ: ܬܠܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܰܡܘܽܕ̈ܶܐ: ܘܰܪܩܰܥ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܣܛܘܽܢ̈ܶܐ. ܟܰܢܶܫ ܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܒܩܰܝܒ̈ܳܬܳܐ:
34. For great are the works of God, deep and hidden are His thoughts. He suspended the heaven without pillars, and extended the earth without supports. He gathered the waters into receptacles; the winds and storms in


[p. 657] {#po.0.p657}


[p. 658] {#po.0.p658}
ܚܒܰܫ ܘܚܰܒܶܫ ܥܰܠܺܝܠܶܐ ܒܙܰܘ̈ܨܪܰܝ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ. ܡܬܰܚ ܪܩܺܝܥܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܡܨܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܦܘܽܪܫܳܢܳܐ ܒܶܝܬ ܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܠܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ: ܦܪܰܫ ܝܰܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܝܰܡܳܐ: ܩܒܰܥ ܢܰܗܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܒܰܪܩܝܺܥܳܐ: ܙܩܰܦ ܛܘܳܪܶܐ ܥܰܠ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܦܪܰܫ ܐܺܝܡܳܡܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܠܶܠܝܳܐ: ܘܢܰܗܝܺܪܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܚܶܫܘܽܟܳܐ: ܘܩܰܝܛܐ ܡܶܢ ܣܰܬܘܳܐ: ܐܶܣܰܪ ܚܳܠܳܐ ܬܚܘܽܡܳܐ ܠܝܰܡܳܐ:
their treasuries He enclosed by His nod. He expanded the firmament in the middle, that it might divide the waters from the waters; He separated the dry land from the sea, fixed the luminaries to the firmament, raised the mountains above the earth, distinguished day from night, light from darkness, summer from winter. He thickened the sand that it might become a boundary for the sea, and enclosed the seas with the ocean; and the waves do not transgress the boundary. The sun proceeds without feet, the moon is moved in a changeable course, clouds fly over without feathers, the wind breathes without wings, and the waves run down lacking a soul. The earth
ܙܩܺܝܦܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܪܝܺܝܢ ܬܚܘܽܡܳܐ: ܡܗܰܠܶܟ݂ ܫܶܡܫܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܓܠܶܐ: ܘܪܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܣܰܗܪܳܐ ܒܚܘܽܠܳܦܳܐ: ܪܳܗܛܺܝܢ ܥܢܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܦ݁ܶܐ: ܘܢܳܫܒܺܝܢ ܪܘܽܚܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܟܶܢ̈ܦܶܐ: ܘܪܳܕ݂ܶܝܢ ܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ. ܬܠܶܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ: ܘܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܟܢܝܺܫܺܝܢ ܒܫܶܬܶܐܣܶܐ. ܠܰܝܬ ܚܙܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܠܪܘܽܚܳܐ: ܠܰܝܬ ܓܶܫܬܳܐ ܠܰܐܐܰܪ: ܠܰܝܬ ܕܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܕܝܰܡܳܐ ܘܰܐܡܺܝܪܺܝܢ ܬܰܢ̈ܺܝܢܶܐ ܕܰܒܔܰܘܶܗ. ܦܫܰܛܺܝܢ ܟܶܢ̈ܦܶܐ ܬܰܪܥܺܝܬܳܐ ܘܰܦܪܝܺܣܺܝܢ ܪܶܓܠܺܝܢ ܘܰܡܨܰܕܶܝܢ ܥܰܝܢܰܝ ܬܺܐܪܬܳܐ ܘܛܳܝܒܺܝܢ ܒܳܒܳܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܰܫܡܰܥܬܳܐ ܠܡܶܡܚܪܙܳܐ ܘܰܠܡܶܥܒܰܕ ܥܘܽܩܳܒܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܕܰܪܟܝܺܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܣܘܽܢ̈ܳܟܶܐ܀
is suspended by the waters, and the waters are gathered into foundations. The spirit is not seen, nor is the air touched; the heavens do not provide a form, nor are the clouds known. Strong are the beasts of the sea, and the wonderful whales which it contains. And the mind unfolds its feathers, thought expands its wings, the senses of the soul scrutinize, the eyes of conscience intend, and the ears attend, that by investigating they may discern and be taught; but they cannot reach the extreme ends.
ܡܰܢܘܽ ܐܰܪܓ݁ܺܫ ܐܰܬܰܪ ܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܢܘܽ ܐܰܬܰܟ ܫܶܪ̈ܫܰܝ ܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ܆ ܘܡܰܢܘܽ ܡܶܬܒܰܚܰܢ ܐܰܬܰܪ ܣܘܽܟܳܠܳܐ. ܟܣܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܚܰܝ̈ܳܢ ܘܡܶܢ ܡܰܚܫ̈ܒܳܢ ܕܟܽܠ ܒܣܰܪ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܙܕܰܒܢܳܐ
35. Who has discovered the seat of knowledge? who has reached the roots of wisdom, or obtained the place of prudence? This is hidden from all the living and from the thoughts of all flesh. Nor will men of dull

[p. 660] {#po.0.p660}
ܒܕ݂ܰܗܒ݁ܳܐ ܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܥܰܛܠ̈ܶܐ: ܦܬܝܺܚ ܘܰܟܒܝܺܩ ܓܰܝܪܳܗ ܠܥܳܐܘܳܠܶܐ. ܡܫܰܬܰܪ ܢܘܽܗܪܳܗ ܡܶܢ ܫܶܡܫܳܐ: ܘܙܰܗܪܶܗ ܦܐܶܐ ܘܰܗܕ݁ܝܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܣܰܗܪܳܐ.
intellect compare it to gold, but its treasure is opened to those who seek and is permitted entirely. Its light surpasses the sun, and its splendor shines more pleasantly and clearly than the moon. The intimacies of the mind touch it, and the senses of thought obtain it,
ܠܳܗ ܕܳܓܫܰܝ ܡܰܚܫܰܒܬܳܐ: ܘܳܪܬܝܺܢ ܠܳܗ ܬܰܘܬܳܪܰܝ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܳܐ. ܕܰܦܬܝܺܚ ܬ݁ܪܰܥ ܠܳܒ݁ܶܗ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܠܳܗ: ܘܰܕ݂ܦܺܝܪܶܣ ܓܶܦ݁ܰܝ ܬܰܪܥܝܳܬܶܗ ܢܳܝܪܶܐ ܠܳܗ. ܫܳܪܝܳܐ ܒܒܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܫܝܺܪܳܐ: ܘܡܶܬܢܰܨܒܳܐ ܒܓ݂ܰܘ ܠܶܒܶܗ ܕܚܰܟܝܺܡܳܐ. ܓܰܕ݂ܪ̈ܰܝܗ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܪܪܝܺܢ ܒܡܰܒ̈ܘܽܥܶܝܗ: ܘܩܳܢܶܐ ܒܳܗ ܣܝܺܡܬܳܐ ܛܡܝܺܪܬܳܐ. ܡܟܰܝܪܳܐ ܡܰܚܫܰܒܬܶܗ ܠܟܽܠ ܙܰܘܡܝܢ: ܘܡܶܬܬܰܚܬܝܳܐ ܡܰܪܢܝܳܬ݁ܶܗ ܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܥܘܽܡܩ̈ܝܢ. ܨܳܝܪܳܐ ܒܓ݂ܰܘ ܠܶܒܶܗ ܬܡܝܳܗܳܬܳܐ: ܘܚܳܙܝܳܢ ܥܰܝܢܰܝ
and the treasure of the soul possesses it itself. He who opens the door of the heart will find it, he who extends the feathers of the mind will enjoy it. It dwells in the prudent man, and is inserted into the heart of the wise. The roots of this [man] are strengthened by the fountains of that, and he possesses the treasure hidden in it. His thought is carried to more sublime things, and his soul descends into the highest. With an intimate heart he fashions wonders, and with the sharpness of the mind he sees the ends of the sea. He comprehends all created things by thought, and his intellect is dilated for receiving. He becomes a great temple of his Creator; the King of the heavenly ones enters into him and dwells, raises his mind to the heights, and lifts his thought to the seat of His holiness, and opens all kinds of treasures to him. His soul is abstracted by contemplation, his heart is captivated by all that it perceives. Things which he had not known are
ܒܡܰܚܫܰܒܬ݁ܶܗ ܟ݀ܽܠ ܟܶܢܪ̈ܝܳܢ: ܘܰܪܘܺܝܚ ܗܘ ܢܰܨܪܶܗ ܕܰܢܩܰܒܶܠ. ܗܰܝܟܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܪܰܒܳܐ ܕܥܳܒܘܽܕܶܗ: ܘܥܳܐܶܠ ܘܟܳܐܶܪ ܒܶܗ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܪܰܘܡܳܐ: ܡܥܰܠܶܐ ܠܳܗ ܠܬܰܪܥܝܳܬܶܗ ܠܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܰܡܦ݁ܰܪܰܚ ܡܰܚܫܰܒܬܶܗ ܠܒܶܝܬ ܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܶܗ ܘܰܡܚܰܝܘܶܐ ܠܳܗ ܓܰܙܳܐ ܕܟ݁ܽܠ ܓܰܝܘܽܢܳܢ. ܘܦ݁ܳܗܶܐ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ ܒܰܚܙܳܬ݂ܳܐ: ܡܶܫܬܒܶܝܐ ܠܶܗ ܠܶܒܶܗ ܠܟܠ ܪܶܓܰܫܘܗ̱ܝ: ܘܰܡܚܰܝܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ܂ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܺܝܕ݂ܰܥ. ܚܳܝܰܪ ܒܝܗܰܘ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ
manifested to him. He looks into that place and contemplates; his mind, whatever

ܘܡܶܬܒܰܝܫܶܐ: ܘܰܐܡܳܗ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ ܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܚܳܙܶܐ: ܪܳܗܛܝܺܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܥܳܕ̈ܶܐ ܒܬܶܫܡܫܬ݁ܶܗ ܘܰܣܬ݁ܳܦ݁ܺܝܐ ܡܩܰܝܕ݂ܘܬܳܐ ܠܬܰܝܩܳܪܶܗ: ܦܳܪܚܝܺܢ ܒܓܶܦ݁ܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܩܰܠܝܺܠܶܐ ܘܚܶܘܳܪܝܺܢ ܘܰܗܕܝܰܪܝܺܢ ܠܒܘܽܫ̈ܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ: ܡܟܰܣܺܝܢ ܐܰܦܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܙܝܳܗܶܗ: ܘܩܰܠܝܰܠܝܺܢ ܪܰܗܛܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܺܚܳܐ. ܡܬܰܩܰܢ ܐܰܡܳܢ ܬܪܽܘܢܳܣ ܕܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܡܥܰܬ݁ܰܕ݂ ܕܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܒܫܶܬ ܕܺܝܢܳܝܐ: ܬܪܝܺܨܝܺܢ ܠܙܰܕ݁ܺܝܩܶܐ ܟܘܽܪ̈ܣܰܘܳܢ ܕܪܳܝܡܝܺܢ ܠܥܰܘܳܠܶܐ ܒܝܰܘܡ ܕܺܝܢܳܝܐ. ܡܳܐ ܕܚܳܙܶܐ ܚܰܟܝܺܡܳܐ ܒܕܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕܣܝܳܡܳܬܶܗ ܣܰܓܺܝܐܳܢ:
it beholds, admires: all the angels hastening to His service, the Seraphim proclaiming His holy glory, flying with swift wings, clothed in white and illustrious garments, veiling their faces before His brightness, and running swifter than the wind. There the throne of the kingdom is established, and the judge is prepared on the tribunal; seats are placed for the just, who will judge the impious on the day of judgment. When, therefore, the wise man contemplates with his mind the place where the multitude of treasures [is stored], then he lifts himself up in spirit, and conceives and brings forth all goods in his heart. He meditates on all things which have been commanded to him. His figure and appearance [exist] on earth, but the senses of his mind [are turned] upward and downward. His thought is swifter than the sun, and its rays are faster than the wind, like the lightest feather they [are carried] in every direction. The wise man in his thoughts
ܘܡܰܘܠܰܕ݂ ܠܶܒܶܗ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܛܳܒ̈ܳܢ: ܘܪܳܢܶܝܐ ܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܐܶܬܦܰܩܺܝܕ݂. ܕܘܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܰܚܙܳܬܶܗ ܥܰܠ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܪܶܓ݂ܫܰܝ ܬܰܪܥܝܺܬܶܗ ܠܥܶܝܠ ܘܰܠܬܰܚܬ. ܩܰܠܝܺܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܡܰܚܫܰܒܬܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܫܶܡܫܳܐ: ܘܦܳܪܚܝܺܢ ܙܰܠܝܺܩܶܝܗ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܐܶܒܪܳܐ ܩܰܠܝܺܠܳܐ ܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܓܰܒ̈ܝܢ. ܡܫܰܪܰܪ ܚܰܟܝܺܡܳܐ ܒܡܰܚܫܰܒܬܶܗ: ܙܥܘܽܪ ܒ݁ܰܚܙܳܬ݂ܶܗ ܘܰܡܟܰܨܰܪ: ܘܰܢܣܝܺܟ ܘܰܡܠܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܓܰܙܶܐ ܥܰܬܝܳܢܳܐ. ܒܠܰܠܝܳܐ ܚܶܫܘܽܟܳܝܐ ܡܶܬܢܰܗܰܪ: ܘܰܡܥܰܝܕܰܪ ܪܶܕܝܳܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܟ݂ܽܠ ܓܰܒ̈ܝܢ: ܓ݁ܳܫܳܐ ܬܰܪܥܝܳܬܶܗ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܫܳܬܶܣܶܐ ܘܰܡܝܬܝܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܓܰܙܳܐ ܕܝܺܕ݁ܰܥܬܳܐ. ܕܠܳܐ ܫܡܰܥ ܐܶܕ݂ܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܗܘܽ ܚܳܝܙܶܐ: ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܚܙܰܝ̈ ܥܰܝܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܗܘܽ ܪܳܓܶܫ. ܥܳܒܪܳܐ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܝܰܡܺܝܢ ܡܰܪܢܺܝܬܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܚܫܺܝܒܺܝܢ ܠܶܗ ܓ݁ܰܕ݁ܺܝܠܶܐ
is stable, in his own eyes vile and cast away, and is filled with the excessive treasure infused into him. The darkness of night is illuminated; he carries his senses wherever he goes; his mind explores all foundations, and provides him with the riches of knowledge. He sees what he does not grasp with his ears, and perceives what he does not discern with his eyes. His thought traverses all the seas, counting the vehement waves as nothing; without

ܬܰܩܺܝܦܶܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܠܦܳܝܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܘܡܰܠܳܚܳܝܐ ܬܰܪܥܝܳܬܶܗ. ܪܰܒ ܘܰܡܝܰܬܰܪ ܓ݁ܰܙܳܐ ܕܬܶܐܓܘܽܪܬܶܗ. ܟܰܕ݂ ܝܳܗܶܒ ܡܶܢ ܕܝܽܠܶܗ ܠܳܐ ܚܳܣܰܪ: ܘܥܳܬܪܝܺܢ

ܠܪܰܠܝܳܢܶܗ ܕܰܩܦܺܝܣ ܘܟܳܪܶܐ ܒܓ݂ܰܘ ܥܘܽܒܶܗ. ܐܰܝܟܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܟܳܝܐ ܫܳܪܶܐ ܘܡܶܫܬܰܡܰܫ ܡܰܢܘܽ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܚܳܫܶܒ ܠܳܟ ܓܰܙܰܘ̈ܗܝ܆ ܣܰܓܺܝܐܳܢ ܥܰܠܽܠܳܬ݂ܶܗ ܘܢܶܦ݁ܺܩܳܬܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܣܢܺܝܩܘܽܬܳܐ܀

ܫܡܰܥܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܚܰܒܺܝܒܰܝܢ ܕܡܰܥܗܕܺܝܢܰܢ ܚ̱ܢܰܢ ܢܰܦܫ̈ܰܢ ܘܐܳܦ ܠܟܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܒ݁ܰܪ̈ܝܳܬ݂ܳܗ ܕ݁ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܥܳܒܕ݁ܳܢ ܛܝܳܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܥܰܨܝ̈ܳܢ ܦܘܽܩܕܳܢܶܝܗ. ܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܚܕ݂ܳܐ
36. Listen, however, most beloved, to that which we relate to you and to ourselves alike: how indeed all the creatures of God follow His will, and do not refuse His command. Each of them, as it has been decreed to them, quickly performs His will; men, however, sometimes do not obey, and refuse to execute the will of God,
ܩܰܠܺܝܠܳܐܝܺܬ ܕܶܒܚܺܝܢܶܝܗ ܣܳܥܪܳܐ: ܘܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܢܫܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܚܙܳܬܰܢ ܙܒܰܢ ܙܒܰܢ ܡܝܰܨܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܕ݁ܺܝܢ ܒܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܳܙܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܫܳܡܥܝܺܢ ܘܠܐ ܡܶܣܬܰܟܠܝܺܢ. ܚܰܝܣܶܕ݂ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܳܝܐ ܒܚܰܝܕ݂ ܐܶܪܰܡܝܳܐ ܠܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܺܝܣܪܳܝܶܠ ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܡܶܢܝ ܠܰܡ ܠܳܐ ܬ݂ܶܕ݂ܚܠܘܿܢ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܘܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡܰܝ ܠܳܐ ܬܙܘܽܥܘܽܢ܆ ܕܣܳܡܶܬ ܚܺܝܠܳܐ ܬܚܘܽܡܳܐ ܠܚܰܝܡܳܐ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܠܥܳܠܰܡ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܰܪ ܠܶܝܗ: ܘܡܶܬܬܰܟܬܰܫ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟܰܚ: ܘܡܶܬܬܪܝܺܡܳܢ ܓܰܠ̱ܠܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܪܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ. ܘܰܠܥܰܡܳܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܠܶܒܳܐ
not seeing, nor hearing, nor understanding. For the Most Holy rebukes the sons of Israel through Jeremiah, saying: Will you not then fear me, says the Lord, and will you not tremble before my face, who have set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an everlasting command; and it does not pass beyond it; it struggles, but it cannot, and its waves swell, and they will not pass it.
